    96→
    97→def make_unused_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[dict]:
    98→    """Transform raw unused-detector entries into normalized findings.
    99→
   100→    Shared by both Python and TypeScript unused phases.
   101→    """
   102→    results = []
   103→    for e in entries:
   104→        tier = 1 if e["category"] == "imports" else 2
   105→        results.append(make_finding(
   106→            "unused", e["file"], e["name"],
   107→            tier=tier, confidence="high",
   108→            summary=f"Unused {e['category']}: {e['name']}",
   109→            detail={"line": e["line"], "category": e["category"]},
   110→        ))
   111→    stderr_fn(f"         {len(entries)} instances -> {len(results)} findings")
   112→    return results
   113→
   114→
   115→def make_dupe_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[dict]:
   116→    """Transform clustered duplicate entries into normalized findings.
   117→
   118→    Each entry represents a cluster of similar functions. One finding per cluster.
   119→    """
   120→    results = []
   121→    for e in entries:
   122→        a, b = e["fn_a"], e["fn_b"]
   123→        if a["loc"] < 10 and b["loc"] < 10:
   124→            continue
   125→        cluster_size = e.get("cluster_size", 2)
   126→        pair = sorted([(a["file"], a["name"]), (b["file"], b["name"])])
   127→        name = f"{pair[0][1]}::{rel(pair[1][0])}::{pair[1][1]}"
   128→        tier = 2 if e["kind"] == "exact" else 3
   129→        conf = "high" if e["kind"] == "exact" else "low"
   130→        kind_label = "Exact" if e["kind"] == "exact" else "Near"
   131→        if cluster_size > 2:
   132→            summary = (f"{kind_label} dupe cluster ({cluster_size} functions, "
   133→                       f"{e['similarity']:.0%} similar): "
   134→                       f"{a['name']} ({rel(a['file'])}:{a['line']}), "
   135→                       f"{b['name']} ({rel(b['file'])}:{b['line']}), ...")
   136→        else:
   137→            summary = (f"{kind_label} dupe: "
   138→                       f"{a['name']} ({rel(a['file'])}:{a['line']}) <-> "
   139→                       f"{b['name']} ({rel(b['file'])}:{b['line']}) [{e['similarity']:.0%}]")
   140→        results.append(make_finding(
   141→            "dupes", pair[0][0], name,
   142→            tier=tier, confidence=conf,
   143→            summary=summary,
   144→            detail={"fn_a": a, "fn_b": b,
   145→                    "similarity": e["similarity"], "kind": e["kind"],
   146→                    "cluster_size": cluster_size,
   147→                    "cluster": e.get("cluster", [a, b])},
   148→        ))
   149→    suppressed = sum(1 for e in entries
   150→                     if e["fn_a"]["loc"] < 10 and e["fn_b"]["loc"] < 10)
   151→    stderr_fn(f"         {len(entries)} clusters, {suppressed} suppressed (<10 LOC)")
   152→    return results
   153→
   154→
   155→def add_structural_signal(structural: dict, file: str, signal: str, detail: dict):
   156→    """Add a complexity signal to the per-file structural dict.
   157→
   158→    Accumulates signals per file so they can be merged into tiered findings.
   159→    """
   160→    f = resolve_path(file)
   161→    structural.setdefault(f, {"signals": [], "detail": {}})
   162→    structural[f]["signals"].append(signal)
   163→    structural[f]["detail"].update(detail)
   164→
   165→
   166→def merge_structural_signals(structural: dict, stderr_fn,
   167→                              *, complexity_only_min: int = 35) -> list[dict]:
   168→    """Convert per-file structural signals into tiered findings.
   169→
   170→    3+ signals -> T4/high (needs decomposition).
   171→    1-2 signals -> T3/medium.
   172→    Complexity-only files (no large/god signals) need score >= complexity_only_min
   173→    to be flagged — lower complexity in small files is normal, not decomposition-worthy.
   174→    """
   175→    results = []
   176→    suppressed = 0
   177→    for filepath, data in structural.items():
   178→        if "loc" not in data["detail"]:
   179→            try:
   180→                p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   181→                data["detail"]["loc"] = len(p.read_text().splitlines())
   182→            except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   183→                data["detail"]["loc"] = 0
   184→
   185→        # Suppress complexity-only findings below the elevated threshold
   186→        signals = data["signals"]
   187→        is_complexity_only = all(s.startswith("complexity") for s in signals)
   188→        if is_complexity_only:
   189→            score = data["detail"].get("complexity_score", 0)
   190→            if score < complexity_only_min:
   191→                suppressed += 1
   192→                continue
   193→
   194→        signal_count = len(signals)
   195→        tier = 4 if signal_count >= 3 else 3
   196→        confidence = "high" if signal_count >= 3 else "medium"
   197→        summary = "Needs decomposition: " + " / ".join(signals)
   198→        results.append(make_finding(
   199→            "structural", filepath, "",
   200→            tier=tier, confidence=confidence,
   201→            summary=summary,
   202→            detail=data["detail"],
   203→        ))
   204→    if suppressed:
   205→        stderr_fn(f"         {suppressed} complexity-only files below threshold (< {complexity_only_min})")
   206→    stderr_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} structural findings")
   207→    return results
   208→
   209→
   210→def make_single_use_findings(
   211→    entries: list[dict],
   212→    get_area,
   213→    *,
   214→    loc_range: tuple[int, int] = (50, 200),
   215→    suppress_colocated: bool = True,
   216→    skip_dir_names: set[str] | None = None,
   217→    stderr_fn,
   218→) -> list[dict]:
   219→    """Filter and normalize single-use entries into findings.
   220→
   221→    Suppresses entries within the LOC range (they're appropriately-sized abstractions),
   222→    entries co-located with their sole importer, and entries in skip_dir_names
   223→    directories (e.g., commands/ — CLI modules are single-use by design).
   224→    """
   225→    results = []
   226→    colocated_suppressed = 0
   227→    lo, hi = loc_range
   228→    for e in entries:
   229→        if lo <= e["loc"] <= hi:
   230→            continue
   231→        # Skip files in directories that are single-use by design (e.g., commands/)
   232→        if skip_dir_names:
   233→            parts = Path(e["file"]).parts
   234→            if any(p in skip_dir_names for p in parts):
   235→                continue
   236→        if suppress_colocated and get_area:
   237→            src_area = get_area(rel(e["file"]))
   238→            imp_area = get_area(e["sole_importer"])
   239→            if src_area == imp_area:
   240→                colocated_suppressed += 1
   241→                continue
   242→        results.append(make_finding(
   243→            "single_use", e["file"], "",
   244→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   245→            summary=f"Single-use ({e['loc']} LOC): only imported by {e['sole_importer']}",
   246→            detail={"loc": e["loc"], "sole_importer": e["sole_importer"]},
   247→        ))
   248→    suppressed = len(entries) - len(results)
   249→    coloc_note = f", {colocated_suppressed} co-located" if colocated_suppressed else ""
   250→    stderr_fn(f"         single-use: {len(entries)} found, {suppressed} suppressed "
   251→              f"({lo}-{hi} LOC{coloc_note})")
   252→    return results
   253→
   254→
   255→def make_cycle_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[dict]:
   256→    """Normalize import cycles into findings."""
   257→    results = []
   258→    for cy in entries:
   259→        cycle_files = [rel(f) for f in cy["files"]]
   260→        name = "::".join(cycle_files[:4])
   261→        if len(cycle_files) > 4:
   262→            name += f"::+{len(cycle_files) - 4}"
   263→        tier = 3 if cy["length"] <= 3 else 4
   264→        results.append(make_finding(
   265→            "cycles", cy["files"][0], name,
   266→            tier=tier, confidence="high",
   267→            summary=f"Import cycle ({cy['length']} files): "
   268→                    + " -> ".join(cycle_files[:5])
   269→                    + (f" -> +{len(cycle_files) - 5}" if len(cycle_files) > 5 else ""),
   270→            detail={"files": cycle_files, "length": cy["length"]},
   271→        ))
   272→    if entries:
   273→        stderr_fn(f"         cycles: {len(entries)} import cycles")
   274→    return results
   275→
   276→
   277→def make_orphaned_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[dict]:
   278→    """Normalize orphaned file entries into findings."""
   279→    results = []
   280→    for e in entries:
   281→        results.append(make_finding(
   282→            "orphaned", e["file"], "",
   283→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   284→            summary=f"Orphaned file ({e['loc']} LOC): zero importers, not an entry point",
   285→            detail={"loc": e["loc"]},
   286→        ))
   287→    if entries:
   288→        stderr_fn(f"         orphaned: {len(entries)} files with zero importers")
   289→    return results
   290→
   291→
   292→SMELL_TIER_MAP = {"high": 2, "medium": 3, "low": 3}
   293→
   294→
   295→def make_smell_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[dict]:
   296→    """Group smell entries by file and assign tiers from severity.
   297→
   298→    Input: list of smell dicts from detect_smells, each with id/label/severity/matches.
   299→    Output: findings grouped per (file, smell_id).
   300→    """
   301→    from collections import defaultdict
   302→    results = []
   303→    for e in entries:
   304→        by_file: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
   305→        for m in e["matches"]:
   306→            by_file[m["file"]].append(m)
   307→        for file, matches in by_file.items():
   308→            conf = "medium" if e["severity"] != "low" else "low"
   309→            tier = SMELL_TIER_MAP.get(e["severity"], 3)
   310→            results.append(make_finding(
   311→                "smells", file, e["id"],
   312→                tier=tier, confidence=conf,
   313→                summary=f"{len(matches)}x {e['label']}",
   314→                detail={"smell_id": e["id"], "severity": e["severity"],
   315→                        "count": len(matches),
   316→                        "lines": [m["line"] for m in matches[:10]]},
   317→            ))
   318→    stderr_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} smell findings")
   319→    return results
   320→
   321→
   322→def phase_dupes(path: Path, lang: LangConfig) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   323→    """Shared phase runner: detect duplicate functions via lang.extract_functions.
   324→
   325→    When a zone map is available, filters out functions from zone-excluded files
   326→    before the O(n^2) comparison to avoid test/config/generated false positives.
   327→    """
   328→    from ..detectors.dupes import detect_duplicates
   329→    from ..utils import log
   330→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
   331→
   332→    # Filter out functions from zone-excluded files
   333→    if lang._zone_map is not None:
   334→        from ..zones import EXCLUDED_ZONES
   335→        before = len(functions)
   336→        functions = [f for f in functions
   337→                     if lang._zone_map.get(getattr(f, "file", "")) not in EXCLUDED_ZONES]
   338→        excluded = before - len(functions)
   339→        if excluded:
   340→            log(f"         zones: {excluded} functions excluded (non-production)")
   341→
   342→    entries, total_functions = detect_duplicates(functions)
   343→    findings = make_dupe_findings(entries, log)
   344→    return findings, {"dupes": total_functions}
   345→
   346→
   347→def make_passthrough_findings(
   348→    entries: list[dict],
   349→    name_key: str,
   350→    total_key: str,
   351→    stderr_fn,
   352→) -> list[dict]:
   353→    """Normalize passthrough detection results into findings."""
   354→    results = []
   355→    for e in entries:
   356→        label = e[name_key]
   357→        results.append(make_finding(
   358→            "props", e["file"], f"passthrough::{label}",
   359→            tier=e["tier"], confidence=e["confidence"],
   360→            summary=f"Passthrough: {label} "
   361→                    f"({e['passthrough']}/{e[total_key]} forwarded, {e['ratio']:.0%})",
   362→            detail={k: v for k, v in e.items() if k != "file"},
   363→        ))
   364→    if entries:
   365→        stderr_fn(f"         passthrough: {len(entries)} findings")
   366→    return results
   367→

   369→def make_facade_findings(entries: list[dict], stderr_fn) -> list[dict]:
   370→    """Normalize re-export facade entries into findings."""
   371→    results = []
   372→    for e in entries:
   373→        kind = e["kind"]
   374→        if kind == "directory":
   375→            summary = (f"Facade directory ({e['loc']} LOC, {e.get('file_count', '?')} files): "
   376→                       f"all modules are re-exports ({e['importers']} importers)")
   377→        else:
   378→            from_str = ", ".join(e["imports_from"][:3])
   379→            if len(e["imports_from"]) > 3:
   380→                from_str += f", +{len(e['imports_from']) - 3}"
   381→            summary = (f"Re-export facade ({e['loc']} LOC): "
   382→                       f"imports from {from_str} ({e['importers']} importers)")
   383→        results.append(make_finding(
   384→            "facade", e["file"], "",
   385→            tier=2, confidence="high" if e["importers"] == 0 else "medium",
   386→            summary=summary,
   387→            detail={"loc": e["loc"], "importers": e["importers"],
   388→                    "imports_from": e["imports_from"], "kind": kind},
   389→        ))
   390→    if entries:
   391→        stderr_fn(f"         facades: {len(entries)} re-export facade findings")
   392→    return results

1→"""Language registry: auto-detection and lookup."""
     2→
     3→import inspect
     4→from pathlib import Path
     5→from .base import LangConfig
     6→
     7→_registry: dict[str, type] = {}
     8→
     9→REQUIRED_FILES = ["commands.py", "extractors.py"]
    10→REQUIRED_DIRS = ["detectors", "fixers"]
    11→
    12→
    13→def _validate_lang_structure(lang_dir: Path, name: str):
    14→    """Validate that a language plugin has all required files and directories."""
    15→    errors = []
    16→    for f in REQUIRED_FILES:
    17→        if not (lang_dir / f).exists():
    18→            errors.append(f"missing required file: {f}")
    19→    for d in REQUIRED_DIRS:
    20→        if not (lang_dir / d).exists():
    21→            errors.append(f"missing required directory: {d}/")
    22→        elif not (lang_dir / d / "__init__.py").exists():
    23→            errors.append(f"missing {d}/__init__.py")
    24→    if errors:
    25→        raise ValueError(
    26→            f"Language plugin '{name}' ({lang_dir.name}/) has structural issues:\n"
    27→            + "\n".join(f"  - {e}" for e in errors)
    28→        )
    29→
    30→
    31→def register_lang(name: str):
    32→    """Decorator to register a language config module."""
    33→    def decorator(cls):
    34→        module = inspect.getmodule(cls)
    35→        if module and hasattr(module, "__file__"):
    36→            _validate_lang_structure(Path(module.__file__).parent, name)
    37→        _registry[name] = cls
    38→        return cls
    39→    return decorator
    40→
    41→
    42→def get_lang(name: str) -> LangConfig:
    43→    """Get a language config by name."""
    44→    if name not in _registry:
    45→        # Lazy-load language modules to populate registry
    46→        _load_all()
    47→    if name not in _registry:
    48→        available = ", ".join(sorted(_registry.keys()))
    49→        raise ValueError(f"Unknown language: {name!r}. Available: {available}")
    50→    return _registry[name]()
    51→
    52→
    53→def auto_detect_lang(project_root: Path) -> str | None:
    54→    """Auto-detect language from project files.
    55→
    56→    When multiple config files are present (e.g. package.json + pyproject.toml),
    57→    counts actual source files to pick the dominant language instead of relying
    58→    on first-match ordering.
    59→    """
    60→    _load_all()
    61→    candidates = []
    62→    if (project_root / "package.json").exists():
    63→        candidates.append("typescript")
    64→    if ((project_root / "pyproject.toml").exists()
    65→            or (project_root / "setup.py").exists()
    66→            or (project_root / "setup.cfg").exists()):
    67→        candidates.append("python")
    68→    if (project_root / "go.mod").exists():
    69→        candidates.append("go")
    70→    if (project_root / "Cargo.toml").exists():
    71→        candidates.append("rust")
    72→
    73→    # Filter to registered languages only
    74→    candidates = [c for c in candidates if c in _registry]
    75→    if not candidates:
    76→        return None
    77→    if len(candidates) == 1:
    78→        return candidates[0]
    79→
    80→    # Multiple candidates — count source files to pick the dominant one.
    81→    # Uses file_finder from each lang config to respect DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS.
    82→    best, best_count = None, -1
    83→    for lang_name in candidates:
    84→        lang_cfg = _registry[lang_name]()
    85→        if lang_cfg.file_finder:
    86→            count = len(lang_cfg.file_finder(project_root))
    87→        else:
    88→            count = 0
    89→        if count > best_count:
    90→            best, best_count = lang_name, count
    91→    return best
    92→
    93→
    94→def available_langs() -> list[str]:
    95→    """Return list of registered language names."""
    96→    _load_all()
    97→    return sorted(_registry.keys())
    98→
    99→
   100→def _load_all():
   101→    """Import all language modules to trigger registration."""
   102→    import importlib
   103→    lang_dir = Path(__file__).parent
   104→    # Discover .py modules (e.g. lang/rust.py)
   105→    for f in sorted(lang_dir.glob("*.py")):
   106→        if f.name in ("__init__.py", "base.py"):
   107→            continue
   108→        module_name = f.stem
   109→        try:
   110→            importlib.import_module(f".{module_name}", __package__)
   111→        except ImportError:
   112→            pass
   113→    # Discover packages (e.g. lang/typescript/)
   114→    for d in sorted(lang_dir.iterdir()):
   115→        if d.is_dir() and (d / "__init__.py").exists() and not d.name.startswith("_"):
   116→            try:
   117→                importlib.import_module(f".{d.name}", __package__)
   118→            except ImportError:
   119→                pass
   120→

    80→def make_cmd_naming(
    81→    file_finder: Callable, skip_names: set[str],

    83→):
    84→    """Factory: detect naming inconsistencies."""
    85→    def cmd_naming(args):

    87→        kwargs = dict(file_finder=file_finder, skip_names=skip_names)
    88→        if skip_dirs:

    90→        entries, _ = detect_naming_inconsistencies(Path(args.path), **kwargs)
    91→        display_entries(args, entries,
    92→            label="Naming inconsistencies",
    93→            empty_msg="\nNo naming inconsistencies found.",
    94→            columns=["Directory", "Majority", "Minority", "Outliers"],
    95→            widths=[45, 20, 20, 40],
    96→            row_fn=lambda e: [
    97→                e["directory"], f"{e['majority']} ({e['majority_count']})",
    98→                f"{e['minority']} ({e['minority_count']})",
    99→                ", ".join(e["outliers"][:5])
   100→                + (f" (+{len(e['outliers']) - 5})" if len(e["outliers"]) > 5 else "")])

   103→
   104→def make_cmd_facade(build_dep_graph_fn: Callable, lang: str):
   105→    """Factory: detect re-export facades."""
   106→    def cmd_facade(args):
   107→        import json
   108→        from ..detectors.facade import detect_reexport_facades
   109→        graph = build_dep_graph_fn(Path(args.path))
   110→        entries, _ = detect_reexport_facades(graph, lang=lang)
   111→        if getattr(args, "json", False):
   112→            print(json.dumps({"count": len(entries), "entries": [
   113→                {**e, "file": rel(e["file"])} for e in entries
   114→            ]}, indent=2))
   115→            return
   116→        if not entries:
   117→            print(c("\nNo re-export facades found.", "green"))
   118→            return
   119→        file_facades = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == "file"]
   120→        dir_facades = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == "directory"]
   121→        if file_facades:
   122→            print(c(f"\nRe-export facade files: {len(file_facades)}\n", "bold"))
   123→            rows = [[rel(e["file"]), str(e["loc"]), str(e["importers"]),
   124→                     ", ".join(e["imports_from"][:3])] for e in file_facades]
   125→            print_table(["File", "LOC", "Importers", "Re-exports From"], rows, [50, 5, 9, 40])
   126→        if dir_facades:
   127→            print(c(f"\nFacade directories: {len(dir_facades)}\n", "bold"))
   128→            rows = [[rel(e["file"]), str(e.get("file_count", "?")), str(e["importers"])]
   129→                    for e in dir_facades]
   130→            print_table(["Directory", "Files", "Importers"], rows, [50, 6, 9])
   131→    return cmd_facade
   132→
   133→
   134→def make_cmd_smells(detect_smells_fn: Callable):
   135→    """Factory: detect code smells."""
   136→    def cmd_smells(args):
   137→        import json
   138→        entries, _ = detect_smells_fn(Path(args.path))
   139→        if getattr(args, "json", False):
   140→            print(json.dumps({"entries": entries}, indent=2))
   141→            return
   142→        if not entries:
   143→            print(c("No code smells detected.", "green"))
   144→            return
   145→        total = sum(e["count"] for e in entries)
   146→        print(c(f"\nCode smells: {total} instances across {len(entries)} patterns\n", "bold"))
   147→        rows = []
   148→        for e in entries[:getattr(args, "top", 20)]:
   149→            sev_color = {"high": "red", "medium": "yellow", "low": "dim"}.get(e["severity"], "dim")
   150→            rows.append([c(e["severity"].upper(), sev_color), e["label"],
   151→                         str(e["count"]), str(e["files"])])
   152→        print_table(["Sev", "Pattern", "Count", "Files"], rows, [8, 40, 6, 6])
   153→        high = [e for e in entries if e["severity"] == "high"]
   154→        for e in high:
   155→            print(c(f"\n  {e['label']} ({e['count']} instances):", "red"))
   156→            for m in e["matches"][:10]:
   157→                print(f"    {rel(m['file'])}:{m['line']}  {m['content'][:60]}")
   158→    return cmd_smells

     5→from dataclasses import dataclass, field

     7→
     8→
     9→@dataclass
    10→class FunctionInfo:
    11→    """Extracted function/method info for cross-language analysis."""
    12→    name: str
    13→    file: str
    14→    line: int
    15→    end_line: int
    16→    loc: int
    17→    body: str
    18→    normalized: str = ""
    19→    body_hash: str = ""
    20→    params: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    21→
    22→
    23→@dataclass
    24→class ClassInfo:
    25→    """Extracted class/component info for cross-language analysis.
    26→
    27→    For OOP classes: methods/attributes/base_classes are populated directly.
    28→    For React components: metrics holds hook counts (context_hooks, use_effects, etc.).
    29→    """
    30→    name: str
    31→    file: str
    32→    line: int
    33→    loc: int
    34→    methods: list[FunctionInfo] = field(default_factory=list)
    35→    attributes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    37→    metrics: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    38→
    39→
    40→@dataclass
    41→class ComplexitySignal:
    42→    """A complexity signal to detect in source files.
    43→
    44→    Either pattern-based (regex matched per line, counted) or compute-based
    45→    (custom function that analyzes content and returns count + label).
    46→    """
    47→    name: str
    48→    pattern: str | None = None       # regex (None = uses compute fn)
    49→    weight: int = 1
    50→    threshold: int = 0
    51→    compute: Callable | None = None  # (content, lines) -> (count, label) | None
    52→
    53→
    54→@dataclass
    55→class GodRule:
    56→    """A rule for detecting god classes/components.
    57→
    58→    The extract callable pulls a metric from ClassInfo; if it meets the threshold,

    60→    """
    61→    name: str
    62→    description: str
    63→    extract: Callable  # (ClassInfo) -> int
    64→    threshold: int
    65→
    66→
    67→@dataclass
    68→class SmellRule:

    38→        from .utils import PROJECT_ROOT
    39→        detected = auto_detect_lang(PROJECT_ROOT)
    40→        lang = get_lang(detected or "typescript")
    41→    return _generate_findings_from_lang(path, lang, include_slow=include_slow,

    45→def _generate_findings_from_lang(
    46→    path: Path, lang, *, include_slow: bool = True,

    52→    # Build zone map if language has zone rules

    54→        from .zones import FileZoneMap, ZONE_POLICIES
    55→        from .utils import rel
    56→        files = lang.file_finder(path)
    57→        lang._zone_map = FileZoneMap(files, lang.zone_rules, rel_fn=rel,
    58→                                      overrides=zone_overrides)
    59→        counts = lang._zone_map.counts()
    60→        zone_str = ", ".join(f"{z}: {n}" for z, n in sorted(counts.items()) if n > 0)
    61→        stderr(f"  Zones: {zone_str}")
    62→
    63→    phases = lang.phases

    67→    findings: list[dict] = []

    69→    total = len(phases)
    70→    for i, phase in enumerate(phases):

    95→def _plan_header(state: dict, stats: dict) -> list[str]:

   102→    if obj_score is not None:

   113→    lines = [

   126→        lines.append(f"\n{total_files} files · {loc_str} LOC · {total_dirs} directories\n")
   127→
   128→    return lines

   131→def _plan_dimension_table(state: dict) -> list[str]:
   132→    """Build the dimension health table rows (empty list when no data)."""
   133→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   134→    if not dim_scores:
   135→        return []
   136→
   137→    lines = [
   138→        "## Health by Dimension",

   151→        strict_val = ds.get("strict", score_val)
   152→        bold = "**" if score_val < 93 else ""
   153→        lines.append(
   154→            f"| {bold}{dim.name}{bold} | T{dim.tier} | "
   155→            f"{checks:,} | {issues} | {score_val:.1f}% | {strict_val:.1f}% |"

   161→def _plan_tier_sections(findings: dict) -> list[str]:
   162→    """Build per-tier sections listing open findings grouped by file."""
   163→    open_findings = [f for f in findings.values() if f["status"] == "open"]
   164→    by_tier_file: dict[int, dict[str, list]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
   165→    for f in open_findings:
   166→        by_tier_file[f["tier"]][f["file"]].append(f)
   167→
   168→    lines: list[str] = []
   169→    for tier_num in [1, 2, 3, 4]:

   171→        if not tier_files:
   172→            continue
   173→        label = TIER_LABELS.get(tier_num, f"Tier {tier_num}")
   174→        tier_count = sum(len(fs) for fs in tier_files.values())
   175→        lines.extend([
   176→            "---",
   177→            f"## Tier {tier_num}: {label} ({tier_count} open)",
   178→            "",
   179→        ])
   180→
   181→        # Sort files by finding count (most findings first)
   182→        sorted_files = sorted(tier_files.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[1]))
   183→        for filepath, file_findings in sorted_files:
   184→            # Sort findings within file: high confidence first
   185→            file_findings.sort(key=lambda f: (CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(f["confidence"], 9), f["id"]))
   186→            lines.append(f"### `{filepath}` ({len(file_findings)} findings)")
   187→            lines.append("")
   188→            for f in file_findings:
   189→                conf_badge = f"[{f['confidence']}]"
   190→                lines.append(f"- [ ] {conf_badge} {f['summary']}")
   191→                lines.append(f"      `{f['id']}`")
   192→            lines.append("")
   193→
   194→    return lines

   197→def generate_plan_md(state: dict) -> str:
   198→    """Generate a prioritized markdown plan from state."""
   199→    findings = state["findings"]
   200→    stats = state.get("stats", {})
   201→
   202→    lines = _plan_header(state, stats)
   203→    lines.extend(_plan_dimension_table(state))
   204→
   205→    # Tier breakdown summary
   206→    by_tier = stats.get("by_tier", {})
   207→    for tier_num in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
   208→        ts = by_tier.get(str(tier_num), {})
   209→        t_open = ts.get("open", 0)
   210→        t_total = sum(ts.values())
   211→        t_addressed = t_total - t_open
   212→        pct = round(t_addressed / t_total * 100) if t_total else 100
   213→        label = TIER_LABELS.get(tier_num, f"Tier {tier_num}")
   214→        lines.append(f"- **Tier {tier_num}** ({label}): {t_open} open / {t_total} total ({pct}% addressed)")
   215→    lines.append("")
   216→
   217→    # Per-tier open finding sections
   218→    lines.extend(_plan_tier_sections(findings))
   219→
   220→    # Addressed findings summary
   221→    addressed = [f for f in findings.values() if f["status"] != "open"]
   222→    if addressed:
   223→        by_status: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   224→        for f in addressed:
   225→            by_status[f["status"]] += 1
   226→        lines.extend([
   227→            "---",
   228→            "## Addressed",
   229→            "",
   230→        ])
   231→        for status, count in sorted(by_status.items()):
   232→            lines.append(f"- **{status}**: {count}")
   233→
   234→        # Show wontfix items with their reasons
   235→        wontfix = [f for f in addressed if f["status"] == "wontfix" and f.get("note")]
   236→        if wontfix:
   237→            lines.extend(["", "### Wontfix (with explanations)", ""])
   238→            for f in wontfix[:30]:
   239→                lines.append(f"- `{f['id']}` — {f['note']}")
   240→        lines.append("")
   241→
   242→    return "\n".join(lines)
   243→
   244→
   245→def get_next_item(state: dict, tier: int | None = None) -> dict | None:
   246→    """Get the highest-priority open finding."""
   247→    items = get_next_items(state, tier, 1)
   248→    return items[0] if items else None
   249→
   250→
   251→def get_next_items(state: dict, tier: int | None = None, count: int = 1) -> list[dict]:
   252→    """Get the N highest-priority open findings.
   253→
   254→    Priority: tier (ascending) → confidence (high first) → detail count.
   255→    """
   256→    open_findings = [f for f in state["findings"].values() if f["status"] == "open"]
   257→    if tier is not None:
   258→        open_findings = [f for f in open_findings if f["tier"] == tier]
   259→    if not open_findings:
   260→        return []
   261→
   262→    open_findings.sort(key=lambda f: (
   263→        f["tier"],
   264→        CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(f["confidence"], 9),
   265→        -f.get("detail", {}).get("count", 0),
   266→        f["id"],
   267→    ))
   268→    return open_findings[:count]

   214→def _apply_persisted_exclusions(args, state: dict):
   215→    """Merge CLI --exclude with persisted config.exclude, set on utils global."""
   216→    from .utils import set_exclusions, c
   217→
   218→    cli_exclusions = getattr(args, "exclude", None) or []
   219→    persisted = state.get("config", {}).get("exclude", [])
   220→    combined = list(cli_exclusions) + [e for e in persisted if e not in cli_exclusions]
   221→    if combined:
   222→        set_exclusions(combined)
   223→        import sys
   224→        if cli_exclusions:
   225→            print(c(f"  Excluding: {', '.join(combined)}", "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
   226→        else:
   227→            print(c(f"  Excluding (from state): {', '.join(combined)}", "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
   228→

   230→def main():
   231→    parser = create_parser()
   232→    args = parser.parse_args()
   233→
   234→    # Resolve default path from language config if not explicitly provided
   235→    if getattr(args, "path", None) is None:
   236→        lang = _resolve_lang(args)
   237→        if lang:
   238→            args.path = str(PROJECT_ROOT / lang.default_src)
   239→        else:
   240→            args.path = str(DEFAULT_PATH)
   241→
   242→    # Load state once and apply exclusions before any command runs
   243→    sp = _state_path(args)
   244→    from .state import load_state
   245→    state = load_state(sp)
   246→    _apply_persisted_exclusions(args, state)
   247→    args._preloaded_state = state
   248→    args._state_path = sp
   249→
   250→    # Lazy-load command handlers from commands/
   251→    from .commands.scan import cmd_scan

   253→    from .commands.show import cmd_show

    15→def _score_color(score: float, *, muted: bool = False) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    16→    """Color-code a score: deep sage >= 90, mustard 70-90, dusty rose < 70.
    17→
    18→    muted=True returns a desaturated variant for secondary display (strict column).
    19→    """
    20→    if score >= 90:
    21→        base = (88, 129, 87)     # deep sage
    22→    elif score >= 70:
    23→        base = (178, 148, 72)    # warm mustard
    24→    else:
    25→        base = (168, 90, 90)     # dusty rose
    26→    if not muted:
    27→        return base
    28→    # Blend toward warm gray for a secondary feel
    29→    gray = (158, 142, 122)
    30→    return tuple(int(b * 0.55 + g * 0.45) for b, g in zip(base, gray))

    84→def _draw_ornament(draw, cx: int, cy: int, size: int, fill):

    86→    draw.polygon([

    99→def _draw_vert_rule_with_ornament(draw, x: int, y1: int, y2: int, cy: int, line_fill, ornament_fill):

   103→    draw.rectangle((x, cy + gap, x + 1, y2), fill=line_fill)

   107→def _get_project_name() -> str:
   108→    """Get project name from GitHub API, git remote, or directory name.
   109→
   110→    Tries `gh` CLI first for the canonical owner/repo (handles renames and
   111→    transfers). Falls back to parsing the git remote URL, then directory name.
   112→    """
   113→    # Try gh CLI for canonical name (handles username renames, repo transfers)
   114→    try:
   115→        name = subprocess.check_output(
   116→            ["gh", "repo", "view", "--json", "nameWithOwner", "-q", ".nameWithOwner"],
   117→            cwd=str(PROJECT_ROOT), stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True,
   118→            timeout=5,
   119→        ).strip()
   120→        if "/" in name:
   121→            return name
   122→    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
   123→        pass
   124→
   125→    # Fall back to git remote URL parsing
   126→    try:
   127→        url = subprocess.check_output(
   128→            ["git", "config", "--get", "remote.origin.url"],
   129→            cwd=str(PROJECT_ROOT), stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True,
   130→            timeout=5,
   131→        ).strip()
   132→        # SSH: git@github.com:owner/repo.git
   133→        # HTTPS: https://github.com/owner/repo.git
   134→        # HTTPS+token: https://[REDACTED]/owner/repo.git
   135→        if url.startswith("git@") and ":" in url:
   136→            path = url.split(":")[-1]
   137→        else:
   138→            path = "/".join(url.split("/")[-2:])
   139→        return path.removesuffix(".git")
   140→    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError, IndexError,
   141→            subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
   142→        return PROJECT_ROOT.name

   147→_BG_SCORE = (240, 232, 217)
   148→_BG_TABLE = (240, 233, 220)
   149→_BG_ROW_ALT = (234, 226, 212)
   150→_TEXT = (58, 48, 38)

   157→def _draw_left_panel(draw, main_score: float, strict_score: float, project_name: str,
   158→                     lp_left: int, lp_right: int, lp_top: int, lp_bot: int):
   159→    """Draw the left panel: score panel background, title, score, strict, project name."""
   160→    font_title = _load_font(15, serif=True, bold=True)
   161→    font_big = _load_font(42, serif=True, bold=True)
   162→    font_strict_label = _load_font(12, serif=True)
   163→    font_strict_val = _load_font(19, serif=True, bold=True)
   164→    font_project = _load_font(9, serif=True)
   165→
   166→    lp_cx = (lp_left + lp_right) // 2
   167→
   168→    draw.rounded_rectangle(
   169→        (lp_left, lp_top, lp_right, lp_bot),
   170→        radius=_s(4), fill=_BG_SCORE, outline=_BORDER, width=1)
   171→
   172→    # Measure all elements
   173→    title = "DESLOPPIFY SCORE"
   174→    title_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), title, font=font_title)
   175→    title_h = title_bbox[3] - title_bbox[1]
   176→    tw = draw.textlength(title, font=font_title)
   177→
   178→    score_str = f"{main_score:.1f}"
   179→    score_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), score_str, font=font_big)
   180→    score_h = score_bbox[3] - score_bbox[1]
   181→
   182→    strict_label_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "strict", font=font_strict_label)
   183→    strict_val_str = f"{strict_score:.1f}"
   184→    strict_val_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), strict_val_str, font=font_strict_val)
   185→    strict_h = max(strict_label_bbox[3] - strict_label_bbox[1],
   186→                   strict_val_bbox[3] - strict_val_bbox[1])
   187→
   188→    proj_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), project_name, font=font_project)
   189→    proj_h = proj_bbox[3] - proj_bbox[1]
   190→
   191→    # Stack: title → ornament rule → score → strict → project pill
   192→    ornament_gap = _s(7)
   193→    score_gap = _s(6)
   194→    proj_gap = _s(8)
   195→    pill_pad_y = _s(3)
   196→    pill_pad_x = _s(8)
   197→    proj_pill_h = proj_h + 2 * pill_pad_y
   198→    total_h = (title_h + ornament_gap + _s(6) + ornament_gap +
   199→               score_h + score_gap + strict_h + proj_gap + proj_pill_h)
   200→    y0 = (lp_top + lp_bot) // 2 - total_h // 2 + _s(3)
   201→
   202→    # Title
   203→    draw.text((lp_cx - tw / 2, y0 - title_bbox[1]), title, fill=_TEXT, font=font_title)
   204→
   205→    # Ornamental rule
   206→    rule_y = y0 + title_h + ornament_gap
   207→    rule_inset = _s(28)
   208→    _draw_rule_with_ornament(draw, rule_y, lp_left + rule_inset, lp_right - rule_inset,
   209→                             lp_cx, _BORDER, _ACCENT)
   210→
   211→    # Main score
   212→    score_y = rule_y + _s(6) + ornament_gap
   213→    sw = draw.textlength(score_str, font=font_big)
   214→    draw.text((lp_cx - sw / 2, score_y - score_bbox[1]), score_str,
   215→              fill=_score_color(main_score), font=font_big)
   216→
   217→    # Strict label + value
   218→    strict_y = score_y + score_h + score_gap
   219→    sl_w = draw.textlength("strict", font=font_strict_label)
   220→    sv_w = draw.textlength(strict_val_str, font=font_strict_val)
   221→    gap = _s(5)
   222→    strict_x = lp_cx - (sl_w + gap + sv_w) / 2
   223→    draw.text((strict_x, strict_y - strict_label_bbox[1]), "strict", fill=_DIM,
   224→              font=font_strict_label)
   225→    draw.text((strict_x + sl_w + gap, strict_y - strict_val_bbox[1]), strict_val_str,
   226→              fill=_score_color(strict_score, muted=True), font=font_strict_val)

   228→    # Project name in a subtle pill

   231→    pw = draw.textlength(project_name, font=font_project)

   233→    pill_right = lp_cx + pw / 2 + pill_pad_x
   234→    pill_bot = pill_top + proj_pill_h
   235→    draw.rounded_rectangle(
   236→        (pill_left, pill_top, pill_right, pill_bot),
   237→        radius=_s(3), fill=_BG, outline=_BORDER, width=1)
   238→    draw.text((lp_cx - pw / 2, proj_y - proj_bbox[1]), project_name,
   239→              fill=_DIM, font=font_project)

   243→def _draw_right_panel(draw, active_dims: list, row_h: int,
   244→                      table_x1: int, table_x2: int, table_top: int, table_bot: int):
   245→    """Draw the right panel: dimension table with header, rows, alternating tints."""
   246→    font_header = _load_font(10, mono=True)
   247→    font_row = _load_font(11, mono=True)
   248→    rule_gap = _s(4)
   249→    rows_gap = _s(6)
   250→    row_count = len(active_dims)
   251→
   252→    draw.rounded_rectangle(
   253→        (table_x1, table_top, table_x2, table_bot),

   255→
   256→    # Column positions
   257→    col_name = table_x1 + _s(12)
   258→    col_health = table_x2 - _s(118)
   259→    col_strict = table_x2 - _s(52)

   263→    header_h = header_bbox[3] - header_bbox[1]

   265→    # Center table content vertically
   266→    table_content_h = header_h + rule_gap + rows_gap + row_count * row_h
   267→    table_content_top = (table_top + table_bot) // 2 - table_content_h // 2 + _s(2)
   268→
   269→    # Header row
   270→    header_y = table_content_top
   271→    draw.text((col_name, header_y - header_bbox[1]), "Dimension", fill=_DIM, font=font_header)
   272→    draw.text((col_health, header_y - header_bbox[1]), "Health", fill=_DIM, font=font_header)
   273→    draw.text((col_strict, header_y - header_bbox[1]), "Strict", fill=_DIM, font=font_header)
   274→
   275→    # Header underline
   276→    line_y = header_y + header_h + rule_gap
   277→    draw.rectangle((col_name, line_y, table_x2 - _s(12), line_y), fill=_BORDER)
   278→

   280→    sample_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), "Xg", font=font_row)
   281→    row_text_h = sample_bbox[3] - sample_bbox[1]
   282→    row_text_offset = sample_bbox[1]
   283→
   284→    y_band = line_y + rows_gap
   285→    for i, (name, data) in enumerate(active_dims):
   286→        band_top = y_band
   287→        band_bot = y_band + row_h
   288→        if i % 2 == 1:
   289→            draw.rectangle((table_x1 + 1, band_top, table_x2 - 1, band_bot), fill=_BG_ROW_ALT)
   290→        text_y = band_top + (row_h - row_text_h) // 2 - row_text_offset + _s(1)
   291→        score = data.get("score", 100)
   292→        strict = data.get("strict", score)
   293→        draw.text((col_name, text_y), name, fill=_TEXT, font=font_row)
   294→        draw.text((col_health, text_y), f"{score:.1f}%", fill=_score_color(score), font=font_row)
   295→        draw.text((col_strict, text_y), f"{strict:.1f}%",
   296→                  fill=_score_color(strict, muted=True), font=font_row)
   297→        y_band += row_h

   300→def generate_scorecard(state: dict, output_path: str | Path) -> Path:
   301→    """Render a landscape scorecard PNG from scan state. Returns the output path."""
   302→    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw  # noqa: deferred — Pillow is optional
   303→
   304→    output_path = Path(output_path)
   305→    dim_scores = state.get("dimension_scores", {})
   306→    obj_score = state.get("objective_score")
   307→    obj_strict = state.get("objective_strict")
   308→
   309→    main_score = obj_score if obj_score is not None else state.get("score", 0)
   310→    strict_score = obj_strict if obj_strict is not None else state.get("strict_score", 0)
   311→
   312→    project_name = _get_project_name()
   313→
   314→    # Layout — landscape (wide), File health first
   315→    active_dims = [(name, data) for name, data in dim_scores.items()
   316→                   if data.get("checks", 0) > 0]
   317→    active_dims.sort(key=lambda x: (0 if x[0] == "File health" else 1, x[0]))
   318→    row_count = len(active_dims)
   319→    row_h = _s(22)
   320→    divider_x = _s(248)
   321→    W = _s(620)
   322→    frame_inset = _s(5)
   323→
   324→    # Height driven by whichever side is taller
   325→    rule_gap = _s(4)
   326→    rows_gap = _s(6)
   327→    table_content_h = _s(14) + rule_gap + rows_gap + row_count * row_h
   328→    content_h = max(table_content_h + _s(28), _s(150))
   329→    H = _s(12) + content_h
   330→
   331→    img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), _BG)
   332→    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
   333→
   334→    # Double frame
   335→    draw.rectangle((0, 0, W - 1, H - 1), outline=_FRAME, width=_s(2))
   336→    draw.rectangle((frame_inset, frame_inset, W - frame_inset - 1, H - frame_inset - 1),
   337→                   outline=_BORDER, width=1)
   338→
   339→    content_top = frame_inset + _s(1)
   340→    content_bot = H - frame_inset - _s(1)
   341→    content_mid_y = (content_top + content_bot) // 2
   342→
   343→    # Left panel: title + score + project name
   344→    _draw_left_panel(draw, main_score, strict_score, project_name,
   345→                     lp_left=frame_inset + _s(6), lp_right=divider_x - _s(8),
   346→                     lp_top=content_top + _s(4), lp_bot=content_bot - _s(4))
   347→
   348→    # Vertical divider with ornament
   349→    _draw_vert_rule_with_ornament(draw, divider_x, content_top + _s(12), content_bot - _s(12),
   350→                                  content_mid_y, _BORDER, _ACCENT)
   351→
   352→    # Right panel: dimension table
   353→    _draw_right_panel(draw, active_dims, row_h,
   354→                      table_x1=divider_x + _s(10), table_x2=W - frame_inset - _s(6),
   355→                      table_top=content_top + _s(4), table_bot=content_bot - _s(4))
   356→
   357→    img.save(str(output_path), "PNG", optimize=True)
   358→    return output_path
   359→
   360→
   361→def get_badge_config(args) -> tuple[Path | None, bool]:
   362→    """Resolve badge output path and whether badge generation is disabled.
   363→
   364→    Returns (output_path, disabled). Checks CLI args, then env vars.
   365→    """
   366→    disabled = getattr(args, "no_badge", False) or os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_NO_BADGE", "").lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")
   367→    if disabled:
   368→        return None, True
   369→    path_str = getattr(args, "badge_path", None) or os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_BADGE_PATH", "scorecard.png")
   370→    path = Path(path_str)
   371→    if not path.is_absolute():
   372→        path = PROJECT_ROOT / path
   373→    return path, False
   374→

    20→def _collect_file_data(path: Path, lang=None) -> list[dict]:
    21→    """Collect LOC for all source files using the language's file finder."""
    22→    if lang and lang.file_finder:
    23→        source_files = lang.file_finder(path)
    24→    else:
    25→        from .utils import find_ts_files
    26→        source_files = find_ts_files(path)
    27→    files = []
    28→    for filepath in source_files:
    29→        try:
    30→            p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
    31→            content = p.read_text()
    32→            loc = len(content.splitlines())
    33→            files.append({
    34→                "path": rel(filepath),
    35→                "abs_path": str(p.resolve()),
    36→                "loc": loc,
    37→            })
    38→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    39→            continue
    40→    return files
    41→
    42→
    43→def _build_tree(files: list[dict], dep_graph: dict, findings_by_file: dict) -> dict:
    44→    """Build nested tree structure for D3 treemap."""
    45→    root: dict = {"name": "src", "children": {}}
    46→
    47→    for f in files:
    48→        parts = f["path"].split("/")
    49→        # Skip leading 'src/' since root is already 'src'
    50→        if parts and parts[0] == "src":
    51→            parts = parts[1:]
    52→        node = root
    53→        for part in parts[:-1]:
    54→            if part not in node["children"]:
    55→                node["children"][part] = {"name": part, "children": {}}
    56→            node = node["children"][part]
    57→
    58→        filename = parts[-1]
    59→        resolved = f["abs_path"]
    60→        dep_entry = dep_graph.get(resolved, {"import_count": 0, "importer_count": 0})
    61→        file_findings = findings_by_file.get(f["path"], [])
    62→        open_findings = [ff for ff in file_findings if ff.get("status") == "open"]
    63→
    64→        node["children"][filename] = {
    65→            "name": filename,
    66→            "path": f["path"],
    67→            "loc": max(f["loc"], 1),  # D3 needs >0 values
    68→            "fan_in": dep_entry.get("importer_count", 0),
    69→            "fan_out": dep_entry.get("import_count", 0),
    70→            "findings_total": len(file_findings),
    71→            "findings_open": len(open_findings),
    72→            "finding_summaries": [ff.get("summary", "") for ff in open_findings[:20]],
    73→        }
    74→
    75→    # Convert children dicts to arrays (D3 format)
    76→    def to_array(node):
    77→        if "children" in node and isinstance(node["children"], dict):
    78→            children = list(node["children"].values())
    79→            for child in children:
    80→                to_array(child)
    81→            node["children"] = children
    82→            # Remove empty directories
    83→            node["children"] = [c for c in node["children"]
    84→                                if "loc" in c or ("children" in c and c["children"])]
    85→    to_array(root)
    86→    return root

   162→# ── Text tree (LLM-readable) ────────────────────────────────
   163→
   164→def _aggregate(node: dict) -> dict:
   165→    """Compute aggregate stats for a tree node."""
   166→    if "children" not in node:
   167→        return {
   168→            "files": 1,
   169→            "loc": node.get("loc", 0),
   170→            "findings": node.get("findings_open", 0),
   171→            "max_coupling": node.get("fan_in", 0) + node.get("fan_out", 0),
   172→        }
   173→    agg = {"files": 0, "loc": 0, "findings": 0, "max_coupling": 0}
   174→    for child in node["children"]:
   175→        child_agg = _aggregate(child)
   176→        agg["files"] += child_agg["files"]
   177→        agg["loc"] += child_agg["loc"]
   178→        agg["findings"] += child_agg["findings"]
   179→        agg["max_coupling"] = max(agg["max_coupling"], child_agg["max_coupling"])
   180→    return agg
   181→
   182→
   183→def _print_tree(node: dict, indent: int, max_depth: int, min_loc: int,
   184→                sort_by: str, detail: bool, lines: list[str]):
   185→    """Recursively print annotated tree."""
   186→    prefix = "  " * indent
   187→
   188→    if "children" not in node:
   189→        # Leaf file
   190→        loc = node.get("loc", 0)
   191→        if loc < min_loc:
   192→            return
   193→        findings = node.get("findings_open", 0)
   194→        coupling = node.get("fan_in", 0) + node.get("fan_out", 0)
   195→        parts = []
   196→        parts.append(f"{loc:,} LOC")
   197→        if findings > 0:
   198→            parts.append(f"⚠{findings}")
   199→        if coupling > 10:
   200→            parts.append(f"c:{coupling}")
   201→        lines.append(f"{prefix}{node['name']}  ({', '.join(parts)})")
   202→
   203→        # Detail: show finding summaries under the file
   204→        if detail and node.get("finding_summaries"):
   205→            for s in node["finding_summaries"]:
   206→                lines.append(f"{prefix}  → {s}")
   207→        return
   208→
   209→    # Directory
   210→    agg = _aggregate(node)
   211→    if agg["loc"] < min_loc:
   212→        return
   213→
   214→    lines.append(f"{prefix}{node['name']}/  ({agg['files']} files, {agg['loc']:,} LOC, {agg['findings']} findings)")
   215→
   216→    if indent >= max_depth:
   217→        return
   218→
   219→    # Sort children
   220→    children = node["children"]
   221→    if sort_by == "findings":
   222→        children = sorted(children, key=lambda c: -_aggregate(c)["findings"])
   223→    elif sort_by == "coupling":
   224→        children = sorted(children, key=lambda c: -_aggregate(c)["max_coupling"])
   225→    else:  # loc (default)
   226→        children = sorted(children, key=lambda c: -_aggregate(c)["loc"])
   227→
   228→    for child in children:
   229→        _print_tree(child, indent + 1, max_depth, min_loc, sort_by, detail, lines)
   230→

   233→                       max_depth: int = 2, focus: str | None = None,
   234→                       min_loc: int = 0, sort_by: str = "loc",
   235→                       detail: bool = False, lang=None) -> str:

   238→    Args:
   239→        path: Directory to scan.
   240→        state: Desloppify state (for findings overlay).
   241→        max_depth: How many levels deep to show.
   242→        focus: Focus on a subdirectory (e.g. 'shared/components/MediaLightbox').
   243→        min_loc: Hide files/dirs below this LOC threshold.
   244→        sort_by: 'loc', 'findings', or 'coupling'.
   245→        detail: Show finding summaries under each file.
   246→        lang: Language config for file discovery and dep graph.
   247→    """
   248→    files = _collect_file_data(path, lang)
   249→    dep_graph = {}
   250→    if lang and lang.build_dep_graph:
   251→        dep_graph = lang.build_dep_graph(path)
   252→    elif not lang:
   253→        try:
   254→            from .lang.typescript.deps import build_dep_graph
   255→            dep_graph = build_dep_graph(path)
   256→        except (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError):
   257→            pass
   258→
   259→    findings_by_file: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
   260→    if state and state.get("findings"):
   261→        for f in state["findings"].values():
   262→            findings_by_file[f["file"]].append(f)
   263→
   264→    tree = _build_tree(files, dep_graph, findings_by_file)
   265→
   266→    # Navigate to focus if specified
   267→    root = tree
   268→    if focus:
   269→        parts = focus.strip("/").split("/")
   270→        # Strip leading 'src' if present (root is already 'src')
   271→        if parts and parts[0] == "src":
   272→            parts = parts[1:]
   273→        for part in parts:
   274→            found = None
   275→            for child in root.get("children", []):
   276→                if child["name"] == part:
   277→                    found = child
   278→                    break
   279→            if found is None:
   280→                return f"Directory not found: {focus}"
   281→            root = found
   282→
   283→    lines: list[str] = []
   284→    _print_tree(root, 0, max_depth, min_loc, sort_by, detail, lines)
   285→    return "\n".join(lines)
   286→
   287→
   288→def cmd_tree(args):
   289→    """Print annotated codebase tree to terminal."""
   290→    from .state import load_state
   291→    from .cli import _resolve_lang
   292→
   293→    path = Path(args.path)
   294→    lang = _resolve_lang(args)
   295→    state = None
   296→    try:
   297→        state = load_state(Path(args.state) if getattr(args, "state", None) else None)
   298→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   299→        pass
   300→
   301→    max_depth = getattr(args, "depth", 2)
   302→    focus = getattr(args, "focus", None)
   303→    min_loc = getattr(args, "min_loc", 0)
   304→    sort_by = getattr(args, "sort", "loc")
   305→    detail = getattr(args, "detail", False)
   306→
   307→    print(generate_tree_text(path, state, max_depth=max_depth, focus=focus,
   308→                             min_loc=min_loc, sort_by=sort_by, detail=detail, lang=lang))

   375→<script>
   376→const data = __TREE_DATA__;
   377→const chartEl = document.getElementById('chart');
   378→const tooltip = document.getElementById('tooltip');
   379→const breadcrumbEl = document.getElementById('breadcrumb');
   380→function esc(s) { const d = document.createElement('div'); d.textContent = s; return d.innerHTML; }
   381→const colorSelect = document.getElementById('colorMode');
   382→
   383→// Color scales
   384→const cruftScale = d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateRdYlGn).domain([10, 0]);
   385→const couplingScale = d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateYlOrRd).domain([0, 40]);
   386→const locScale = d3.scaleSequential(d3.interpolateBlues).domain([0, 800]);
   387→
   388→let colorMode = 'findings';
   389→
   390→function getColor(d) {
   391→  if (!d.data.loc) return '#21262d';
   392→  const dd = d.data;
   393→  if (colorMode === 'findings') return cruftScale(Math.min(dd.findings_open || 0, 10));
   394→  if (colorMode === 'coupling') return couplingScale(Math.min((dd.fan_in||0) + (dd.fan_out||0), 40));
   395→  if (colorMode === 'loc') return locScale(Math.min(dd.loc||0, 800));
   396→  return '#21262d';
   397→}
   398→
   399→function isLightBg(color) {
   400→  const c = d3.color(color);
   401→  return c ? (c.r * 0.299 + c.g * 0.587 + c.b * 0.114) > 140 : false;
   402→}
   403→
   404→// Build D3 hierarchy
   405→const root = d3.hierarchy(data)
   406→  .sum(d => d.loc || 0)
   407→  .sort((a, b) => (b.value || 0) - (a.value || 0));
   408→
   409→let currentFocus = root;
   410→
   411→const svg = d3.select('#chart').append('svg');
   412→
   413→function getSize() {
   414→  return [chartEl.clientWidth, chartEl.clientHeight];
   415→}
   416→
   417→function render(focus) {
   418→  currentFocus = focus;
   419→  const [W, H] = getSize();
   420→  svg.attr('width', W).attr('height', H);
   421→
   422→  // Layout this subtree
   423→  d3.treemap()
   424→    .size([W, H])
   425→    .paddingTop(d => d === focus ? 0 : 18)
   426→    .paddingRight(2).paddingBottom(2).paddingLeft(2)
   427→    .paddingInner(1)
   428→    .round(true)(focus);
   429→
   430→  svg.selectAll('*').remove();
   431→
   432→  // Breadcrumb
   433→  const ancestors = focus.ancestors().reverse();
   434→  breadcrumbEl.innerHTML = ancestors.map((a, i) =>
   435→    i < ancestors.length - 1
   436→      ? `<span data-depth="${i}">${esc(a.data.name)}</span>`
   437→      : `<strong>${esc(a.data.name)}</strong>`
   438→  ).join(' / ');
   439→
   440→  if (!focus.children) return;
   441→
   442→  // Render each immediate child
   443→  focus.children.forEach(child => {
   444→    if (child.children) {
   445→      renderDir(child);
   446→    } else {
   447→      renderLeaf(svg, child);
   448→    }
   449→  });
   450→}
   451→
   452→function renderDir(dir) {
   453→  const w = dir.x1 - dir.x0;
   454→  const h = dir.y1 - dir.y0;
   455→  if (w < 3 || h < 3) return;
   456→
   457→  const g = svg.append('g');
   458→
   459→  // Directory background
   460→  g.append('rect')
   461→    .attr('x', dir.x0).attr('y', dir.y0)
   462→    .attr('width', w).attr('height', h)
   463→    .attr('fill', '#161b22')
   464→    .attr('stroke', '#30363d').attr('stroke-width', 0.5)
   465→    .attr('rx', 2)
   466→    .style('cursor', 'pointer')
   467→    .on('click', () => render(dir))
   468→    .on('mouseenter', e => showDirTooltip(e, dir))
   469→    .on('mousemove', moveTooltip)
   470→    .on('mouseleave', hideTooltip);
   471→
   472→  // Directory label
   473→  if (w > 30) {
   474→    const maxChars = Math.floor((w - 8) / 7);
   475→    const label = dir.data.name.length > maxChars
   476→      ? dir.data.name.slice(0, maxChars - 1) + '…'
   477→      : dir.data.name;
   478→    g.append('text')
   479→      .attr('x', dir.x0 + 4).attr('y', dir.y0 + 13)
   480→      .attr('fill', '#8b949e').attr('font-size', '11px').attr('font-weight', 500)
   481→      .style('pointer-events', 'none')
   482→      .text(label + '/');
   483→  }
   484→
   485→  // Render all leaf descendants
   486→  const leaves = dir.descendants().filter(d => !d.children);
   487→  leaves.forEach(leaf => renderLeaf(g, leaf));
   488→}
   489→
   490→function renderLeaf(parent, d) {
   491→  const w = d.x1 - d.x0;
   492→  const h = d.y1 - d.y0;
   493→  if (w < 2 || h < 2) return;
   494→
   495→  const color = getColor(d);
   496→  parent.append('rect')
   497→    .attr('x', d.x0).attr('y', d.y0)
   498→    .attr('width', w).attr('height', h)
   499→    .attr('fill', color)
   500→    .attr('stroke', '#0d1117').attr('stroke-width', 0.5)
   501→    .attr('rx', 1)
   502→    .style('cursor', 'pointer')
   503→    .on('click', e => { e.stopPropagation(); })
   504→    .on('mouseenter', e => showFileTooltip(e, d))
   505→    .on('mousemove', moveTooltip)
   506→    .on('mouseleave', hideTooltip);
   507→
   508→  // File name label
   509→  if (w > 30 && h > 14) {
   510→    const name = d.data.name.replace(/\.(tsx?|jsx?)$/, '');
   511→    const maxChars = Math.floor((w - 6) / 6);
   512→    const label = name.length > maxChars ? name.slice(0, maxChars - 1) + '…' : name;
   513→    parent.append('text')
   514→      .attr('x', d.x0 + 3).attr('y', d.y0 + 11)
   515→      .attr('fill', isLightBg(color) ? '#0d1117' : '#e6edf3')
   516→      .attr('font-size', '10px').attr('font-weight', 600)
   517→      .style('pointer-events', 'none')
   518→      .text(label);
   519→  }
   520→}
   521→
   522→// Tooltips
   523→function showFileTooltip(event, d) {
   524→  const dd = d.data;
   525→  let html = `<div class="tt-path">${esc(dd.path || dd.name)}</div><div class="tt-stats">`;
   526→  html += `<strong>${(dd.loc||0).toLocaleString()}</strong> LOC`;
   527→  html += ` · Fan-in: <strong>${dd.fan_in||0}</strong> · Fan-out: <strong>${dd.fan_out||0}</strong>`;
   528→  if (dd.findings_open > 0)
   529→    html += ` · <strong style="color:#f0883e">${dd.findings_open} findings</strong>`;
   530→  html += `</div>`;
   531→  if (dd.finding_summaries && dd.finding_summaries.length) {
   532→    html += `<div class="tt-findings">`;
   533→    dd.finding_summaries.slice(0,5).forEach(s => { html += `<div class="tt-finding">• ${esc(s)}</div>`; });
   534→    if (dd.finding_summaries.length > 5)
   535→      html += `<div class="tt-finding">… +${dd.finding_summaries.length-5} more</div>`;
   536→    html += `</div>`;
   537→  }
   538→  tooltip.innerHTML = html;
   539→  tooltip.style.display = 'block';
   540→  moveTooltip(event);
   541→}
   542→
   543→function showDirTooltip(event, d) {
   544→  const leaves = d.leaves();
   545→  const loc = d3.sum(leaves, l => l.data.loc || 0);
   546→  const findings = d3.sum(leaves, l => l.data.findings_open || 0);
   547→  const path = d.ancestors().reverse().map(a => a.data.name).join('/');
   548→  let html = `<div class="tt-path">${esc(path)}/</div><div class="tt-stats">`;
   549→  html += `<strong>${leaves.length}</strong> files · <strong>${loc.toLocaleString()}</strong> LOC`;
   550→  if (findings > 0) html += ` · <strong style="color:#f0883e">${findings} findings</strong>`;
   551→  html += `</div>`;
   552→  tooltip.innerHTML = html;
   553→  tooltip.style.display = 'block';
   554→  moveTooltip(event);
   555→}
   556→
   557→function moveTooltip(e) {
   558→  let x = e.clientX + 12, y = e.clientY + 12;
   559→  if (x + 380 > window.innerWidth) x = e.clientX - 380;
   560→  if (y + 180 > window.innerHeight) y = e.clientY - 180;
   561→  tooltip.style.left = x + 'px';
   562→  tooltip.style.top = y + 'px';
   563→}
   564→
   565→function hideTooltip() { tooltip.style.display = 'none'; }
   566→
   567→// Breadcrumb click → navigate up
   568→breadcrumbEl.addEventListener('click', e => {
   569→  const span = e.target.closest('span[data-depth]');
   570→  if (!span) return;
   571→  const depth = parseInt(span.dataset.depth);
   572→  const ancestors = currentFocus.ancestors().reverse();
   573→  if (depth < ancestors.length) render(ancestors[depth]);
   574→});
   575→
   576→// Color mode
   577→colorSelect.addEventListener('change', () => { colorMode = colorSelect.value; render(currentFocus); });
   578→
   579→// Resize
   580→window.addEventListener('resize', () => render(currentFocus));
   581→
   582→// Go
   583→render(root);
   584→</script>
   585→</body>
   586→</html>"""
   587→

  "content": "\"\"\"Tests for desloppify.detectors.graph — iterative Tarjan's SCC cycle detection.\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom desloppify.detectors.graph import detect_cycles\n\n\ndef _make_graph(edges: dict[str, set[str]]) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Build a graph dict from {node: {targets}} mapping.\n\n    Constructs the full graph structure with imports/importers/counts\n    that detect_cycles expects.\n    \"\"\"\n    all_nodes = set(edges.keys())\n    for targets in edges.values():\n        all_nodes.update(targets)\n\n    graph: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for node in all_nodes:\n        graph[node] = {\n            \"imports\": edges.get(node, set()),\n            \"importers\": set(),\n            \"import_count\": 0,\n            \"importer_count\": 0,\n        }\n\n    # Populate importers\n    for node, targets in edges.items():\n        for target in targets:\n            if target in graph:\n                graph[target][\"importers\"].add(node)\n\n    # Compute counts\n    for v in graph.values():\n        v[\"import_count\"] = len(v[\"imports\"])\n        v[\"importer_count\"] = len(v[\"importers\"])\n\n    return graph\n\n\nclass TestDetectCycles:\n    def test_empty_graph(self):\n        entries, total = detect_cycles({})\n        assert entries == []\n        assert total == 0\n\n    def test_acyclic_graph(self):\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"c.py\"},\n            \"c.py\": set(),\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert entries == []\n        assert total == 3\n\n    def test_simple_two_node_cycle(self):\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert len(entries) == 1\n        assert sorted(entries[0][\"files\"]) == [\"a.py\", \"b.py\"]\n        assert entries[0][\"length\"] == 2\n        assert total == 2\n\n    def test_three_node_cycle(self):\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"c.py\"},\n            \"c.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert len(entries) == 1\n        assert sorted(entries[0][\"files\"]) == [\"a.py\", \"b.py\", \"c.py\"]\n        assert entries[0][\"length\"] == 3\n        assert total == 3\n\n    def test_multiple_separate_cycles(self):\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n            \"c.py\": {\"d.py\"},\n            \"d.py\": {\"c.py\"},\n            \"e.py\": set(),\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert len(entries) == 2\n        assert total == 5\n        # Cycles sorted by length descending (both length 2 here)\n        cycle_sets = [set(e[\"files\"]) for e in entries]\n        assert {\"a.py\", \"b.py\"} in cycle_sets\n        assert {\"c.py\", \"d.py\"} in cycle_sets\n\n    def test_self_loop_not_detected(self):\n        \"\"\"Self-loops produce a component of size 1, which is filtered out by Tarjan's.\n\n        The algorithm only reports SCCs with len > 1.\n        \"\"\"\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        # Self-loop creates a component of size 1 — Tarjan's only reports size >= 2\n        assert entries == []\n        assert total == 1\n\n    def test_mixed_cyclic_and_acyclic(self):\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n            \"c.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n            \"d.py\": {\"c.py\"},\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert len(entries) == 1\n        assert sorted(entries[0][\"files\"]) == [\"a.py\", \"b.py\"]\n        assert total == 4\n\n    def test_deferred_imports_skipped_by_default(self):\n        \"\"\"Deferred imports (inside functions) should be excluded from cycle detection.\"\"\"\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        # Mark b.py -> a.py as deferred\n        graph[\"b.py\"][\"deferred_imports\"] = {\"a.py\"}\n\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph, skip_deferred=True)\n        assert entries == []\n\n    def test_deferred_imports_included_when_disabled(self):\n        \"\"\"When skip_deferred=False, deferred imports are included.\"\"\"\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        graph[\"b.py\"][\"deferred_imports\"] = {\"a.py\"}\n\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph, skip_deferred=False)\n        assert len(entries) == 1\n        assert sorted(entries[0][\"files\"]) == [\"a.py\", \"b.py\"]\n\n    def test_edges_only_within_graph(self):\n        \"\"\"Edges pointing to nodes not in the graph should be ignored.\"\"\"\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\", \"external.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        # Remove external.py from graph to simulate it not being a tracked file\n        del graph[\"external.py\"]\n\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert len(entries) == 1\n        assert total == 2\n\n    def test_large_cycle(self):\n        \"\"\"A cycle of many nodes should be detected as one SCC.\"\"\"\n        nodes = [f\"mod_{i}.py\" for i in range(10)]\n        edges = {nodes[i]: {nodes[(i + 1) % 10]} for i in range(10)}\n        graph = _make_graph(edges)\n\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert len(entries) == 1\n        assert entries[0][\"length\"] == 10\n        assert total == 10\n\n    def test_return_format(self):\n        graph = _make_graph({\n            \"a.py\": {\"b.py\"},\n            \"b.py\": {\"a.py\"},\n        })\n        entries, total = detect_cycles(graph)\n        assert isinstance(entries, list)\n        assert isinstance(total, int)\n        entry = entries[0]\n        assert \"files\" in entry\n        assert \"length\" in entry\n        assert isinstance(entry[\"files\"], list)\n        assert isinstance(entry[\"length\"], int)\n"
