   160→                in_string = None
   161→                i += 1
   162→                continue
   163→        i += 1
   164→    return in_string is not None
   165→
   166→
   167→def detect_smells(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   168→    """Detect Python code smell patterns. Returns (entries, total_files_checked)."""
   169→    smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]] = {s["id"]: [] for s in SMELL_CHECKS}
   170→    files = find_py_files(path)
   171→    # Collect module-level constants for cross-file duplicate detection
   172→    constants_by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[tuple[str, int]]] = {}
   173→
   174→    for filepath in files:
   175→        try:
   176→            p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   177→            content = p.read_text()
   178→            lines = content.splitlines()
   179→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   180→            continue
   181→
   182→        # Build set of lines inside multi-line strings to avoid false positives
   183→        multiline_string_lines = _build_string_line_set(lines)
   184→
   185→        for check in SMELL_CHECKS:
   186→            if check["pattern"] is None:
   187→                continue
   188→            for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   189→                # Skip lines inside multi-line strings
   190→                if i in multiline_string_lines:
   191→                    continue
   192→                m = re.search(check["pattern"], line)
   193→                if m and not _match_is_in_string(line, m.start()):
   194→                    # Skip URLs assigned to module-level constants (UPPER_CASE = "https://...")
   195→                    if check["id"] == "hardcoded_url" and re.match(
   196→                        r"^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\s*=", line.strip()
   197→                    ):
   198→                        continue
   199→                    smell_counts[check["id"]].append({
   200→                        "file": filepath, "line": i + 1, "content": line.strip()[:100],
   201→                    })
   202→
   203→        _detect_empty_except(filepath, lines, smell_counts)
   204→        _detect_swallowed_errors(filepath, lines, smell_counts)
   205→        _detect_ast_smells(filepath, content, smell_counts)
   206→        _detect_star_import_no_all(filepath, content, path, smell_counts)
   207→        _collect_module_constants(filepath, content, constants_by_key)
   208→
   209→    # Cross-file: detect duplicate constants
   210→    _detect_duplicate_constants(constants_by_key, smell_counts)
   211→
   212→    severity_order = {"high": 0, "medium": 1, "low": 2}
   213→    entries = []
   214→    for check in SMELL_CHECKS:
   215→        matches = smell_counts[check["id"]]
   216→        if matches:
   217→            entries.append({
   218→                "id": check["id"], "label": check["label"], "severity": check["severity"],
   219→                "count": len(matches), "files": len(set(m["file"] for m in matches)),
   220→                "matches": matches[:50],
   221→            })
   222→    entries.sort(key=lambda e: (severity_order.get(e["severity"], 9), -e["count"]))
   223→    return entries, len(files)
   224→
   225→
   226→def _walk_except_blocks(lines: list[str]):
   227→    """Yield (line_index, except_line_stripped, body_lines) for each except block."""
   228→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   229→        stripped = line.strip()
   230→        if not re.match(r"except\s*(?:\w|\(|:)", stripped) and stripped != "except:":
   231→            continue
   232→        if not stripped.endswith(":"):
   233→            continue
   234→        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
   235→        j, body_lines = i + 1, []
   236→        while j < len(lines):
   237→            next_line = lines[j]
   238→            next_stripped = next_line.strip()
   239→            if next_stripped == "":
   240→                j += 1
   241→                continue
   242→            if len(next_line) - len(next_line.lstrip()) <= indent:
   243→                break
   244→            body_lines.append(next_stripped)
   245→            j += 1
   246→        yield i, stripped, body_lines
   247→
   248→
   249→def _is_broad_except(stripped: str) -> bool:
   250→    """Check if except clause catches broadly (bare, Exception, BaseException)."""
   251→    if stripped == "except:":
   252→        return True
   253→    m = re.match(r"except\s+(\w+)", stripped)
   254→    return bool(m and m.group(1) in ("Exception", "BaseException"))
   255→
   256→
   257→def _detect_empty_except(filepath: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   258→    """Find broad except blocks that just pass or have empty body."""
   259→    for i, stripped, body_lines in _walk_except_blocks(lines):
   260→        if (not body_lines or body_lines == ["pass"]) and _is_broad_except(stripped):
   261→            smell_counts["empty_except"].append({
   262→                "file": filepath, "line": i + 1, "content": stripped[:100],
   263→            })
   264→
   265→
   266→def _detect_swallowed_errors(filepath: str, lines: list[str], smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   267→    """Find except blocks that only print/log the error."""
   268→    _LOG_RE = r"(?:print|logging\.\w+|logger\.\w+|log\.\w+)\s*\("
   269→    for i, stripped, body_lines in _walk_except_blocks(lines):
   270→        if body_lines and all(re.match(_LOG_RE, s) for s in body_lines):
   271→            smell_counts["swallowed_error"].append({
   272→                "file": filepath, "line": i + 1, "content": stripped[:100],
   273→            })
   274→
   275→
   276→def _detect_ast_smells(filepath: str, content: str, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   277→    """Detect AST-based code smells by dispatching to focused detectors."""
   278→    try:
   279→        tree = ast.parse(content)
   280→    except SyntaxError:
   281→        return
   282→
   283→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   284→        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   285→            _detect_monster_functions(filepath, node, smell_counts)
   286→            _detect_dead_functions(filepath, node, smell_counts)
   287→            _detect_deferred_imports(filepath, node, smell_counts)
   288→            _detect_inline_classes(filepath, node, smell_counts)
   289→            _detect_lru_cache_mutable(filepath, node, tree, smell_counts)
   290→
   291→    _detect_subprocess_no_timeout(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   292→    _detect_mutable_class_var(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   293→    _detect_unsafe_file_write(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   294→    _detect_unreachable_code(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   295→    _detect_constant_return(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   296→    _detect_regex_backtrack(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   297→    _detect_naive_comment_strip(filepath, tree, smell_counts)
   298→
   299→
   300→def _detect_monster_functions(filepath: str, node: ast.AST, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   301→    """Flag functions longer than 150 LOC."""
   302→    if not (hasattr(node, "end_lineno") and node.end_lineno):
   303→        return
   304→    loc = node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1
   305→    if loc > 150:
   306→        smell_counts["monster_function"].append({
   307→            "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno, "content": f"{node.name}() — {loc} LOC",
   308→        })
   309→
   310→
   311→def _is_return_none(stmt: ast.AST) -> bool:
   312→    """Check if a statement is `return` or `return None`."""
   313→    if not isinstance(stmt, ast.Return):
   314→        return False
   315→    return stmt.value is None or (isinstance(stmt.value, ast.Constant) and stmt.value.value is None)
   316→
   317→
   318→def _is_docstring(stmt: ast.AST) -> bool:
   319→    return isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr) and isinstance(stmt.value, (ast.Constant, ast.JoinedStr))
   320→
   321→
   322→def _detect_dead_functions(filepath: str, node: ast.AST, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   323→    """Flag functions whose body is only pass, return, or return None."""
   324→    if node.decorator_list:
   325→        return
   326→    body = node.body
   327→    if len(body) == 1:
   328→        stmt = body[0]
   329→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Pass) or _is_return_none(stmt):
   330→            smell_counts["dead_function"].append({
   331→                "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   332→                "content": f"{node.name}() — body is only {ast.dump(stmt)[:40]}",
   333→            })
   334→    elif len(body) == 2:
   335→        first, second = body
   336→        if not _is_docstring(first):
   337→            return
   338→        if isinstance(second, ast.Pass):
   339→            desc = "docstring + pass"
   340→        elif _is_return_none(second):
   341→            desc = "docstring + return None"
   342→        else:
   343→            return
   344→        smell_counts["dead_function"].append({
   345→            "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno, "content": f"{node.name}() — {desc}",
   346→        })
   347→
   348→
   349→def _detect_deferred_imports(filepath: str, node: ast.AST, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   350→    """Flag function-level imports (possible circular import workarounds)."""
   351→    _SKIP_MODULES = ("typing", "typing_extensions", "__future__")
   352→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   353→        if not isinstance(child, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)) or child.lineno <= node.lineno:
   354→            continue
   355→        module = getattr(child, "module", None) or ""
   356→        if module in _SKIP_MODULES:
   357→            continue
   358→        names = ", ".join(a.name for a in child.names[:3])
   359→        if len(child.names) > 3:
   360→            names += f", +{len(child.names) - 3}"
   361→        smell_counts["deferred_import"].append({
   362→            "file": filepath, "line": child.lineno,
   363→            "content": f"import {module or names} inside {node.name}()",
   364→        })
   365→        break  # Only flag once per function
   366→
   367→
   368→def _detect_inline_classes(filepath: str, node: ast.AST, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   369→    """Flag classes defined inside functions."""
   370→    for child in node.body:
   371→        if isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
   372→            smell_counts["inline_class"].append({
   373→                "file": filepath, "line": child.lineno,
   374→                "content": f"class {child.name} defined inside {node.name}()",
   375→            })
   376→
   377→
   378→def _detect_subprocess_no_timeout(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   379→    """Flag subprocess.run/Popen/call/check_call/check_output without timeout=."""
   380→    _SUBPROCESS_FUNCS = {"run", "Popen", "call", "check_call", "check_output"}
   381→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   382→        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   383→            continue
   384→        # Match subprocess.run(...) or subprocess.call(...) etc.
   385→        func = node.func
   386→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _SUBPROCESS_FUNCS:
   387→            # Check if the receiver is 'subprocess'
   388→            if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "subprocess":
   389→                has_timeout = any(kw.arg == "timeout" for kw in node.keywords)
   390→                if not has_timeout:
   391→                    smell_counts["subprocess_no_timeout"].append({
   392→                        "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   393→                        "content": f"subprocess.{func.attr}() without timeout",
   394→                    })
   395→
   396→
   397→def _detect_mutable_class_var(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   398→    """Flag class-level mutable defaults (shared across all instances).
   399→
   400→    Detects: class Foo: data = [] / data = {} / data: list = []
   401→    Skips dataclasses (which use field(default_factory=...)) and __init__ assignments.
   402→    """
   403→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   404→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   405→            continue
   406→        # Skip dataclasses (they handle mutable defaults via field())
   407→        is_dataclass = any(
   408→            (isinstance(d, ast.Name) and d.id == "dataclass") or
   409→            (isinstance(d, ast.Call) and isinstance(d.func, ast.Name) and d.func.id == "dataclass") or
   410→            (isinstance(d, ast.Attribute) and d.attr == "dataclass")
   411→            for d in node.decorator_list
   412→        )
   413→        if is_dataclass:
   414→            continue
   415→
   416→        for stmt in node.body:
   417→            # Plain assignment: data = [] or data = {}
   418→            if isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign):
   419→                if isinstance(stmt.value, (ast.List, ast.Dict, ast.Set)):
   420→                    names = [t.id for t in stmt.targets if isinstance(t, ast.Name)]
   421→                    for name in names:
   422→                        smell_counts["mutable_class_var"].append({
   423→                            "file": filepath, "line": stmt.lineno,
   424→                            "content": f"{node.name}.{name} = {ast.dump(stmt.value)[:40]}",
   425→                        })
   426→            # Annotated assignment: data: list = []
   427→            elif isinstance(stmt, ast.AnnAssign) and stmt.value is not None:
   428→                if isinstance(stmt.value, (ast.List, ast.Dict, ast.Set)):
   429→                    name = stmt.target.id if isinstance(stmt.target, ast.Name) else "?"
   430→                    smell_counts["mutable_class_var"].append({
   431→                        "file": filepath, "line": stmt.lineno,
   432→                        "content": f"{node.name}.{name}: ... = {ast.dump(stmt.value)[:40]}",
   433→                    })
   434→
   435→
   436→def _detect_lru_cache_mutable(filepath: str, node: ast.AST, tree: ast.Module,
   437→                               smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   438→    """Flag @lru_cache/@cache functions that reference module-level mutable variables.
   439→
   440→    Finds globals referenced in the function body that aren't in the parameter list,
   441→    checking if those names are assigned to mutable values at module level.
   442→    """
   443→    # Check if this function has @lru_cache or @cache decorator
   444→    has_cache = False
   445→    for dec in node.decorator_list:
   446→        if isinstance(dec, ast.Name) and dec.id in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   447→            has_cache = True
   448→        elif isinstance(dec, ast.Call) and isinstance(dec.func, ast.Name):
   449→            if dec.func.id in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   450→                has_cache = True
   451→        elif isinstance(dec, ast.Attribute) and dec.attr in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   452→            has_cache = True
   453→    if not has_cache:
   454→        return
   455→
   456→    # Get parameter names
   457→    param_names = set()
   458→    for arg in node.args.args + node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   459→        param_names.add(arg.arg)
   460→    if node.args.vararg:
   461→        param_names.add(node.args.vararg.arg)
   462→    if node.args.kwarg:
   463→        param_names.add(node.args.kwarg.arg)
   464→
   465→    # Collect module-level mutable assignments
   466→    module_mutables = set()
   467→    for stmt in tree.body:
   468→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign):
   469→            for target in stmt.targets:
   470→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and isinstance(stmt.value, (ast.List, ast.Dict, ast.Set, ast.Call)):
   471→                    module_mutables.add(target.id)
   472→        elif isinstance(stmt, ast.AnnAssign) and stmt.target and isinstance(stmt.target, ast.Name):
   473→            if stmt.value and isinstance(stmt.value, (ast.List, ast.Dict, ast.Set, ast.Call)):
   474→                module_mutables.add(stmt.target.id)
   475→
   476→    # Find Name references in function body that point to module-level mutables
   477→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   478→        if isinstance(child, ast.Name) and child.id in module_mutables and child.id not in param_names:
   479→            smell_counts["lru_cache_mutable"].append({
   480→                "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   481→                "content": f"@lru_cache on {node.name}() reads mutable global '{child.id}'",
   482→            })
   483→            return  # One warning per function is enough
   484→
   485→
   486→def _collect_module_constants(filepath: str, content: str,
   487→                              constants_by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[tuple[str, int]]]):
   488→    """Collect module-level constant assignments for cross-file duplicate detection.
   489→
   490→    Only collects UPPER_CASE or _UPPER_CASE names assigned to simple literals
   491→    (dicts, lists, sets, tuples, numbers, strings).
   492→    """
   493→    try:
   494→        tree = ast.parse(content)
   495→    except SyntaxError:
   496→        return
   497→
   498→    for node in tree.body:
   499→        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
   500→            for target in node.targets:
   501→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and re.match(r"^_?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$", target.id):
   502→                    try:
   503→                        value_repr = ast.dump(node.value)
   504→                    except (RecursionError, ValueError):
   505→                        continue
   506→                    if len(value_repr) > 500:
   507→                        continue  # Skip very large constants
   508→                    key = (target.id, value_repr)
   509→                    constants_by_key.setdefault(key, []).append((filepath, node.lineno))
   510→
   511→
   512→def _detect_duplicate_constants(constants_by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[tuple[str, int]]],
   513→                                 smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   514→    """Flag constants defined identically in multiple files."""
   515→    for (name, _value_repr), locations in constants_by_key.items():
   516→        if len(locations) < 2:
   517→            continue
   518→        # Check that locations are in distinct files
   519→        files = set(fp for fp, _ in locations)
   520→        if len(files) < 2:
   521→            continue
   522→        for filepath, lineno in locations:
   523→            other_files = [fp for fp, _ in locations if fp != filepath]
   524→            smell_counts["duplicate_constant"].append({
   525→                "file": filepath,
   526→                "line": lineno,
   527→                "content": f"{name} also defined in {', '.join(Path(f).name for f in other_files[:3])}",
   528→            })
   529→
   530→
   531→def _detect_unsafe_file_write(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   532→    """Flag Path.write_text/write_bytes and open(..., 'w') without atomic pattern.
   533→
   534→    Looks for .write_text() or .write_bytes() calls that aren't preceded by
   535→    a nearby os.replace() or os.rename() call in the same function.
   536→    Also flags open(file, 'w') without evidence of temp+rename.
   537→    """
   538→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   539→        if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   540→            continue
   541→
   542→        # Collect all method calls and check for atomic patterns in this function
   543→        has_atomic_pattern = False
   544→        write_calls: list[ast.Call] = []
   545→
   546→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   547→            if not isinstance(child, ast.Call):
   548→                continue
   549→            func = child.func
   550→
   551→            # Check for os.replace or os.rename (indicates atomic write pattern)
   552→            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in ("replace", "rename"):
   553→                if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "os":
   554→                    has_atomic_pattern = True
   555→
   556→            # Check for shutil.move (also indicates careful file handling)
   557→            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr == "move":
   558→                if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "shutil":
   559→                    has_atomic_pattern = True
   560→
   561→            # Collect .write_text() and .write_bytes() calls
   562→            if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in ("write_text", "write_bytes"):
   563→                write_calls.append(child)
   564→
   565→        # Only flag if no atomic pattern exists in the same function
   566→        if not has_atomic_pattern:
   567→            for call in write_calls:
   568→                smell_counts["unsafe_file_write"].append({
   569→                    "file": filepath, "line": call.lineno,
   570→                    "content": f".{call.func.attr}() in {node.name}() without atomic write pattern",
   571→                })
   572→
   573→
   574→def _detect_unreachable_code(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   575→    """Flag statements after unconditional return/raise/break/continue.
   576→
   577→    Walks every statement block (function body, if/else body, etc.) and flags
   578→    any statement that follows an unconditional flow-control statement.
   579→    """
   580→    _TERMINAL = (ast.Return, ast.Raise, ast.Break, ast.Continue)
   581→
   582→    def _check_block(stmts: list[ast.stmt]):
   583→        for i, stmt in enumerate(stmts):
   584→            if isinstance(stmt, _TERMINAL) and i < len(stmts) - 1:
   585→                next_stmt = stmts[i + 1]
   586→                # Skip flagging string constants (often used as section markers)
   587→                if isinstance(next_stmt, ast.Expr) and isinstance(next_stmt.value, ast.Constant):
   588→                    continue
   589→                smell_counts["unreachable_code"].append({
   590→                    "file": filepath, "line": next_stmt.lineno,
   591→                    "content": f"unreachable after {type(stmt).__name__.lower()} on line {stmt.lineno}",
   592→                })
   593→            # Recurse into compound statements
   594→            for attr in ("body", "orelse", "finalbody", "handlers"):
   595→                block = getattr(stmt, attr, None)
   596→                if isinstance(block, list):
   597→                    child_stmts = [s for s in block if isinstance(s, ast.stmt)]
   598→                    if child_stmts:
   599→                        _check_block(child_stmts)
   600→            # ExceptHandler has a body too
   601→            if isinstance(stmt, ast.ExceptHandler):
   602→                _check_block(stmt.body)
   603→
   604→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   605→        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   606→            _check_block(node.body)
   607→
   608→
   609→def _detect_constant_return(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   610→    """Flag functions that always return the same constant value.
   611→
   612→    Analyzes all return paths — if every return statement returns the same
   613→    literal value (True, False, None, a number, or a string), the function
   614→    likely has dead logic or is a stub masquerading as real code.
   615→    """
   616→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   617→        if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   618→            continue
   619→        # Skip tiny functions (stubs/pass-only already caught by dead_function)
   620→        if not hasattr(node, "end_lineno") or not node.end_lineno:
   621→            continue
   622→        loc = node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1
   623→        if loc < 4:
   624→            continue
   625→        # Skip decorated functions (properties, abstractmethods, etc.)
   626→        if node.decorator_list:
   627→            continue
   628→
   629→        returns = []
   630→        has_conditional = False
   631→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   632→            if isinstance(child, ast.Return):
   633→                returns.append(child)
   634→            if isinstance(child, (ast.If, ast.For, ast.While, ast.With,
   635→                                   ast.Try, ast.ExceptHandler)):
   636→                has_conditional = True
   637→
   638→        # Need at least 2 returns and some conditional logic to be interesting
   639→        if len(returns) < 2 or not has_conditional:
   640→            continue
   641→
   642→        # Extract constant values from all returns
   643→        values = set()
   644→        all_constant = True
   645→        for ret in returns:
   646→            if ret.value is None:
   647→                values.add(repr(None))
   648→            elif isinstance(ret.value, ast.Constant):
   649→                values.add(repr(ret.value.value))
   650→            else:
   651→                all_constant = False
   652→                break
   653→
   654→        if all_constant and len(values) == 1:
   655→            val = next(iter(values))
   656→            # Skip functions that always return None — they're just procedures
   657→            if val == "None":
   658→                continue
   659→            smell_counts["constant_return"].append({
   660→                "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   661→                "content": f"{node.name}() always returns {val} ({len(returns)} return sites)",
   662→            })
   663→
   664→
   665→def _detect_regex_backtrack(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   666→    """Flag regex patterns vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS).
   667→
   668→    Detects nested quantifiers like (a+)+, (a*)*b, ([^)]*|.)*,
   669→    and overlapping alternation inside quantifiers.
   670→    """
   671→    _RE_FUNCS = {"compile", "search", "match", "fullmatch", "findall",
   672→                 "finditer", "sub", "subn", "split"}
   673→    # Nested quantifier: group with inner +/* quantifier, outer +/* quantifier.
   674→    # Only + and * are dangerous — ? (zero-or-one) can never cause ReDoS.
   675→    _NESTED_QUANT = re.compile(
   676→        r"\([^)]*[+*][^)]*\)[+*]"  # (stuff+stuff)+ or (stuff*stuff)*
   677→        r"|"
   678→        r"\(\?:[^)]*[+*][^)]*\)[+*]"  # (?:stuff+stuff)+
   679→    )
   680→
   681→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   682→        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   683→            continue
   684→
   685→        # Match re.X(...) or compiled.X(...)
   686→        func = node.func
   687→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _RE_FUNCS:
   688→            if isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "re":
   689→                pass  # re.compile(...) etc.
   690→            else:
   691→                continue
   692→        elif isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in _RE_FUNCS:
   693→            pass  # Bare compile(...) etc. (rare)
   694→        else:
   695→            continue
   696→
   697→        # Extract pattern string from first arg
   698→        if not node.args:
   699→            continue
   700→        pat_node = node.args[0]
   701→        if not isinstance(pat_node, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(pat_node.value, str):
   702→            continue
   703→        pattern = pat_node.value
   704→
   705→        # Check for nested quantifiers
   706→        m_bt = _NESTED_QUANT.search(pattern)
   707→        if not m_bt:
   708→            continue
   709→
   710→        # Extract the flagged fragment for safety checks
   711→        frag = m_bt.group(0)
   712→
   713→        # Safe: negated character classes [^X]+ can't overlap with adjacent chars
   714→        if re.search(r"\[\^[^\]]+\][+*]", frag):
   715→            continue
   716→
   717→        # Safe: inner quantifier is on a literal-anchored subpattern like \.\w+
   718→        # The required literal prevents ambiguous backtracking
   719→        if re.search(r"\\.\w*[+*]", frag):
   720→            continue
   721→
   722→        smell_counts["regex_backtrack"].append({
   723→            "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   724→            "content": f"pattern: {pattern[:80]}",
   725→        })
   726→
   727→
   728→def _detect_naive_comment_strip(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   729→    """Flag re.sub() calls that strip comments without string awareness.
   730→
   731→    Detects patterns like re.sub(r"//[^\\n]*", "") or re.sub(r"/\\*.*?\\*/", "")
   732→    which corrupt URLs and other legitimate // or /* sequences inside strings.
   733→    """
   734→    _COMMENT_PATTERNS = (
   735→        r"//",           # Line comment stripping
   736→        r"/\*",          # Block comment stripping
   737→        r"#[^\n]",       # Python comment stripping (when applied to non-Python content)
   738→    )
   739→
   740→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   741→        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   742→            continue
   743→        func = node.func
   744→        # Match re.sub(...)
   745→        if not (isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr == "sub"
   746→                and isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) and func.value.id == "re"):
   747→            continue
   748→
   749→        if len(node.args) < 2:
   750→            continue
   751→        pat_node = node.args[0]
   752→        if not isinstance(pat_node, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(pat_node.value, str):
   753→            continue
   754→        pattern = pat_node.value
   755→
   756→        # Check if this is a comment-stripping pattern
   757→        for comment_sig in _COMMENT_PATTERNS:
   758→            if comment_sig in pattern:
   759→                # Check replacement is empty or whitespace
   760→                repl_node = node.args[1]
   761→                if isinstance(repl_node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(repl_node.value, str):
   762→                    if repl_node.value.strip() == "":
   763→                        smell_counts["naive_comment_strip"].append({
   764→                            "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   765→                            "content": f're.sub(r"{pattern[:60]}", "") — not string-aware',
   766→                        })
   767→                        break
   768→
   769→
   770→def _detect_star_import_no_all(filepath: str, content: str, scan_root: Path,
   771→                                smell_counts: dict[str, list]):
   772→    """Flag `from X import *` where the target module has no __all__.
   773→
   774→    Resolves relative and absolute imports within the scan root and checks
   775→    whether the target .py file defines __all__. Only flags targets that
   776→    are part of the scanned project (not stdlib/third-party).
   777→    """
   778→    try:
   779→        tree = ast.parse(content)
   780→    except SyntaxError:
   781→        return
   782→
   783→    file_path = Path(filepath)
   784→    file_dir = file_path.parent
   785→
   786→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   787→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
   788→            continue
   789→        # Only care about star imports
   790→        if not any(alias.name == "*" for alias in node.names):
   791→            continue
   792→
   793→        module = node.module or ""
   794→        level = node.level  # 0 = absolute, 1+ = relative
   795→
   796→        # Resolve to a file path
   797→        target = _resolve_import_target(module, level, file_dir, scan_root)
   798→        if target is None:
   799→            continue
   800→
   801→        # Check if target defines __all__
   802→        try:
   803→            target_content = target.read_text()
   804→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   805→            continue
   806→
   807→        if re.search(r"^__all__\s*=", target_content, re.MULTILINE):
   808→            continue  # Has __all__, controlled export — skip
   809→
   810→        smell_counts["star_import_no_all"].append({
   811→            "file": filepath,
   812→            "line": node.lineno,
   813→            "content": f"from {('.' * level) + module} import * (target has no __all__)",
   814→        })
   815→
   816→
   817→def _resolve_import_target(module: str, level: int, file_dir: Path,
   818→                            scan_root: Path) -> Path | None:
   819→    """Resolve a Python import to a file path within the scan root.
   820→
   821→    Returns the target .py file, or None if unresolvable or outside the project.
   822→    """
   823→    if level > 0:
   824→        # Relative import — go up (level - 1) directories from file_dir
   825→        base = file_dir
   826→        for _ in range(level - 1):
   827→            base = base.parent
   828→    else:
   829→        # Absolute import — start from scan root's parent (package root)
   830→        base = scan_root.parent
   831→
   832→    # Convert module dotted path to filesystem path
   833→    parts = module.split(".") if module else []
   834→    target_dir = base / Path(*parts) if parts else base
   835→
   836→    # Check for package (__init__.py) or module (.py)
   837→    init_path = target_dir / "__init__.py"
   838→    if init_path.is_file():
   839→        return init_path
   840→
   841→    module_path = target_dir.with_suffix(".py")
   842→    if module_path.is_file():
   843→        return module_path
   844→
   845→    return None
   846→

    39→def _levenshtein(s1: str, s2: str) -> int:
    40→    """Compute Levenshtein edit distance between two strings."""
    41→    if len(s1) < len(s2):
    42→        return _levenshtein(s2, s1)
    43→    if len(s2) == 0:
    44→        return len(s1)
    45→    prev = list(range(len(s2) + 1))
    46→    for i, c1 in enumerate(s1):
    47→        curr = [i + 1]
    48→        for j, c2 in enumerate(s2):
    49→            cost = 0 if c1 == c2 else 1
    50→            curr.append(min(curr[j] + 1, prev[j + 1] + 1, prev[j] + cost))
    51→        prev = curr
    52→    return prev[-1]

    55→def _is_singular_plural(a: str, b: str) -> bool:

   110→    def _get_tracked(self, name: str) -> TrackedDict | None:

   338→                    if td:
   339→                        # The left side of `in` for the first op is node.left
   340→                        left = node.left if i == 0 else node.comparators[i - 1]
   341→                        key = _get_str_key(left)
   342→                        if key:
   343→                            td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   344→        self.generic_visit(node)
   345→
   346→    def visit_For(self, node: ast.For):
   347→        """Handle `for x in d` — bulk read."""
   348→        name = _get_name(node.iter)
   349→        if name:
   350→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
   351→            if td:
   352→                td.bulk_read = True
   353→        self.generic_visit(node)
   354→
   355→    def visit_Starred(self, node: ast.Starred):
   356→        """Handle {**d} or func(*d)."""
   357→        name = _get_name(node.value)
   358→        if name:
   359→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
   360→            if td:
   361→                td.has_star_unpack = True
   362→        self.generic_visit(node)
   363→
   364→    # ── Dict literal collection (standalone, non-assigned) ──
   365→
   366→    def visit_Dict(self, node: ast.Dict):
   367→        """Collect dict literals for schema drift analysis."""
   368→        if (all(isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str)
   369→                for k in node.keys if k is not None)
   370→                and len(node.keys) >= 3
   371→                and all(k is not None for k in node.keys)):
   372→            keys = frozenset(k.value for k in node.keys if isinstance(k, ast.Constant))
   373→            self._dict_literals.append({
   374→                "file": self.filepath, "line": node.lineno,
   375→                "keys": keys,
   376→            })
   377→        self.generic_visit(node)
   378→
   379→    # ── Scope analysis ──
   380→
   381→    def _analyze_scope(self, scope: dict[str, TrackedDict], func_name: str,
   382→                       *, is_class: bool = False):
   383→        """Analyze a completed scope for dict key issues."""
   384→        for td in scope.values():
   385→            if not td.locally_created:
   386→                continue
   387→
   388→            # Determine if dead-write warnings should be suppressed
   389→            suppress_dead = (
   390→                td.returned_or_passed
   391→                or td.has_dynamic_key
   392→                or td.has_star_unpack
   393→                or td.bulk_read
   394→                or any(td.name.lower().endswith(n) or td.name.lower() == n
   395→                       for n in _CONFIG_NAMES)
   396→                or (not is_class and func_name in ("__init__", "setUp", "setup"))
   397→                or sum(len(v) for v in td.writes.values()) < 3
   398→            )
   399→
   400→            written_keys = set(td.writes.keys())
   401→            read_keys = set(td.reads.keys())
   402→
   403→            # Dead writes: written but never read
   404→            dead_keys = written_keys - read_keys
   405→            if not suppress_dead:
   406→                for key in sorted(dead_keys):
   407→                    lines = td.writes[key]
   408→                    self._findings.append({
   409→                        "file": self.filepath, "kind": "dead_write",
   410→                        "variable": td.name, "key": key,
   411→                        "line": lines[0], "func": func_name,
   412→                        "tier": 3, "confidence": "medium",
   413→                        "summary": (f'Dict key "{key}" written to `{td.name}` '
   414→                                    f'at line {lines[0]} but never read'),
   415→                        "detail": f"in {func_name}()",
   416→                    })
   417→
   418→            # Phantom reads: read but never written (on locally-created dict)
   419→            phantom_keys = read_keys - written_keys
   420→            for key in sorted(phantom_keys):
   421→                lines = td.reads[key]
   422→                self._findings.append({
   423→                    "file": self.filepath, "kind": "phantom_read",
   424→                    "variable": td.name, "key": key,
   425→                    "line": lines[0], "func": func_name,
   426→                    "tier": 2, "confidence": "high",
   427→                    "summary": (f'Dict key "{key}" read at line {lines[0]} '
   428→                                f'but never written to `{td.name}`'),
   429→                    "detail": (f"Created at line {td.created_line} in "
   430→                               f"{func_name}() — will raise KeyError or "
   431→                               f"return None via .get()"),
   432→                })
   433→
   434→            # Near-miss: dead write key ≈ phantom read key
   435→            for dk in sorted(dead_keys):
   436→                for pk in sorted(phantom_keys):
   437→                    dist = _levenshtein(dk, pk)
   438→                    is_sp = _is_singular_plural(dk, pk)
   439→                    if dist <= 2 or is_sp:
   440→                        write_line = td.writes[dk][0]
   441→                        read_line = td.reads[pk][0]
   442→                        self._findings.append({
   443→                            "file": self.filepath, "kind": "near_miss",
   444→                            "variable": td.name, "key": f"{dk}~{pk}",
   445→                            "line": write_line, "func": func_name,
   446→                            "tier": 2, "confidence": "high",
   447→                            "summary": (f'Possible key typo: "{dk}" vs "{pk}" '
   448→                                        f'on dict `{td.name}` in {func_name}()'),
   449→                            "detail": (f'Written: "{dk}" at line {write_line}, '
   450→                                       f'Read: "{pk}" at line {read_line} '
   451→                                       f'— edit distance {dist}'),
   452→                        })
   453→
   454→            # Overwritten keys: same key assigned twice with no read between
   455→            for key, write_lines in td.writes.items():
   456→                if len(write_lines) < 2:
   457→                    continue
   458→                read_lines = td.reads.get(key, [])
   459→                for i in range(len(write_lines) - 1):
   460→                    w1, w2 = write_lines[i], write_lines[i + 1]
   461→                    # Check if any read of this key occurs between w1 and w2
   462→                    has_read_between = any(w1 < r <= w2 for r in read_lines)
   463→                    if not has_read_between:
   464→                        self._findings.append({
   465→                            "file": self.filepath, "kind": "overwritten_key",
   466→                            "variable": td.name, "key": key,
   467→                            "line": w2, "func": func_name,
   468→                            "tier": 3, "confidence": "medium",
   469→                            "summary": (f'Dict key "{key}" overwritten on `{td.name}` '
   470→                                        f'at line {w2} (previously set at line {w1}, '
   471→                                        f'never read between)'),
   472→                            "detail": f"in {func_name}()",
   473→                        })
   474→
   475→
   476→# ── Pass 1: Single-scope dict key analysis ────────────────
   477→
   478→def detect_dict_key_flow(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   479→    """Walk all .py files, run DictKeyVisitor. Returns (entries, files_checked)."""
   480→    files = find_py_files(path)
   481→    all_findings: list[dict] = []
   482→    all_literals: list[dict] = []
   483→
   484→    for filepath in files:
   485→        try:
   486→            p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   487→            source = p.read_text()
   488→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   489→            continue
   490→
   491→        try:
   492→            tree = ast.parse(source, filename=filepath)
   493→        except SyntaxError:
   494→            continue
   495→
   496→        visitor = DictKeyVisitor(filepath)
   497→        visitor.visit(tree)
   498→        all_findings.extend(visitor._findings)
   499→        all_literals.extend(visitor._dict_literals)
   500→
   501→    return all_findings, len(files)
   502→
   503→
   504→# ── Pass 2: Schema drift clustering ──────────────────────
   505→
   506→def _jaccard(a: frozenset, b: frozenset) -> float:
   507→    if not a and not b:
   508→        return 1.0
   509→    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)
   510→
   511→
   512→def detect_schema_drift(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   513→    """Cluster dict literals by key similarity, report outlier keys.
   514→
   515→    Returns (entries, literals_checked).
   516→    """
   517→    files = find_py_files(path)
   518→    all_literals: list[dict] = []
   519→
   520→    for filepath in files:
   521→        try:
   522→            p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
   523→            source = p.read_text()
   524→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   525→            continue
   526→        try:
   527→            tree = ast.parse(source, filename=filepath)
   528→        except SyntaxError:
   529→            continue
   530→
   531→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   532→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Dict):
   533→                continue
   534→            if len(node.keys) < 3:
   535→                continue
   536→            if not all(isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str)
   537→                       for k in node.keys if k is not None):
   538→                continue
   539→            if any(k is None for k in node.keys):
   540→                continue  # Has **spread
   541→            keys = frozenset(k.value for k in node.keys if isinstance(k, ast.Constant))
   542→            all_literals.append({
   543→                "file": filepath, "line": node.lineno, "keys": keys,
   544→            })
   545→
   546→    if len(all_literals) < 3:
   547→        return [], len(all_literals)
   548→
   549→    # Greedy single-linkage clustering with Jaccard >= 0.8
   550→    clusters: list[list[dict]] = []
   551→    assigned = [False] * len(all_literals)
   552→
   553→    for i, lit in enumerate(all_literals):
   554→        if assigned[i]:
   555→            continue
   556→        cluster = [lit]
   557→        assigned[i] = True
   558→        for j in range(i + 1, len(all_literals)):
   559→            if assigned[j]:
   560→                continue
   561→            # Check similarity against any member in the cluster
   562→            for member in cluster:
   563→                if _jaccard(lit["keys"], all_literals[j]["keys"]) >= 0.8:
   564→                    cluster.append(all_literals[j])
   565→                    assigned[j] = True
   566→                    break
   567→        clusters.append(cluster)
   568→
   569→    # Report outlier keys within clusters of size >= 3
   570→    findings: list[dict] = []
   571→    for cluster in clusters:
   572→        if len(cluster) < 3:
   573→            continue
   574→
   575→        # Build key frequency
   576→        key_freq: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   577→        for member in cluster:
   578→            for k in member["keys"]:
   579→                key_freq[k] += 1
   580→
   581→        # Find consensus keys and outliers
   582→        threshold = 0.3 * len(cluster)
   583→        consensus = {k for k, v in key_freq.items() if v >= threshold}
   584→
   585→        for member in cluster:
   586→            outlier_keys = member["keys"] - consensus
   587→            for ok in outlier_keys:
   588→                # Check if it's close to a consensus key (likely typo)
   589→                close_match = None
   590→                for ck in consensus:
   591→                    dist = _levenshtein(ok, ck)
   592→                    if dist <= 2 or _is_singular_plural(ok, ck):
   593→                        close_match = ck
   594→                        break
   595→
   596→                present = key_freq[ok]
   597→                tier = 2 if len(cluster) >= 5 else 3
   598→                confidence = "high" if len(cluster) >= 5 else "medium"
   599→
   600→                suggestion = f' Did you mean "{close_match}"?' if close_match else ""
   601→                findings.append({
   602→                    "file": member["file"], "kind": "schema_drift",
   603→                    "key": ok, "line": member["line"],
   604→                    "tier": tier, "confidence": confidence,
   605→                    "summary": (f'Schema drift: {len(cluster) - present}/{len(cluster)} '
   606→                                f'dict literals use different key, but '
   607→                                f'{member["file"]}:{member["line"]} uses "{ok}".{suggestion}'),
   608→                    "detail": (f"Cluster of {len(cluster)} similar dict literals. "
   609→                               f'Key "{ok}" appears in only {present}. '
   610→                               f"Consensus keys: {sorted(consensus)}"),
   611→                })
   612→
   613→    return findings, len(all_literals)
   614→

    82→def _resolve_python_from_import(module_path: str, import_names: str, source_file: str, scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
    83→    """Resolve a 'from X import Y' statement to file paths.
    84→
    85→    When module_path is dots-only (e.g. 'from . import X, Y'), each imported
    86→    name might be a submodule, so we resolve each name individually.
    87→    Otherwise, resolve the module_path as before.
    88→    """
    89→    source = Path(source_file) if Path(source_file).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / source_file
    90→    source_dir = source.parent
    91→    scan_root_path = Path(scan_root) if not isinstance(scan_root, Path) else scan_root
    92→
    93→    # Check if module_path is dots-only (no remainder after the dots)
    94→    dots_only = all(ch == "." for ch in module_path)
    95→
    96→    if dots_only:
    97→        # from . import X, Y  or  from .. import X, Y
    98→        # Each imported name could be a submodule in the base directory
    99→        dots = len(module_path)
   100→        base = source_dir
   101→        for _ in range(dots - 1):
   102→            base = base.parent
   103→
   104→        results = []
   105→        # Parse the import names (handle "X, Y" and "X as Z, Y as W")
   106→        names = [n.strip().split()[0] for n in import_names.split(",")]
   107→        for name in names:
   108→            if not name or name.startswith("(") or name.startswith("#"):
   109→                continue
   110→            name = name.strip("()")
   111→            if not name:
   112→                continue
   113→            # Try resolving as a submodule: base/name.py or base/name/__init__.py
   114→            target = _try_resolve_path(base / name)
   115→            if target:
   116→                results.append(target)
   117→
   118→        # Also resolve the package __init__.py itself (from . import X can pull from __init__)
   119→        if not results:
   120→            target = _try_resolve_path(base)
   121→            if target:
   122→                results.append(target)
   123→        return results
   124→    else:
   125→        # Normal case: from .foo import bar, from ..foo.bar import baz
   126→        target = _resolve_python_import(module_path, source_file, scan_root_path)
   127→        return [target] if target else []
   128→
   129→
   130→def _resolve_python_import(module_path: str, source_file: str, scan_root: Path) -> str | None:
   131→    """Resolve a Python import to a file path.
   132→
   133→    Handles:
   134→      - Relative imports (starting with .)
   135→      - Absolute imports within the project
   136→    """
   137→    source = Path(source_file) if Path(source_file).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / source_file
   138→    source_dir = source.parent
   139→    scan_root_path = Path(scan_root) if not isinstance(scan_root, Path) else scan_root
   140→
   141→    if module_path.startswith("."):
   142→        return _resolve_relative_import(module_path, source_dir)
   143→    else:
   144→        return _resolve_absolute_import(module_path, scan_root_path)
   145→
   146→
   147→def _resolve_relative_import(module_path: str, source_dir: Path) -> str | None:
   148→    """Resolve a relative Python import (from . import X, from .foo import X)."""
   149→    # Count leading dots
   150→    dots = 0
   151→    for ch in module_path:
   152→        if ch == ".":
   153→            dots += 1
   154→        else:
   155→            break
   156→
   157→    remainder = module_path[dots:]
   158→
   159→    # Go up (dots - 1) directories from source_dir
   160→    base = source_dir
   161→    for _ in range(dots - 1):
   162→        base = base.parent
   163→
   164→    if remainder:
   165→        parts = remainder.split(".")
   166→        target_base = base
   167→        for part in parts:
   168→            target_base = target_base / part
   169→    else:
   170→        target_base = base
   171→
   172→    return _try_resolve_path(target_base)
   173→
   174→
   175→def _resolve_absolute_import(module_path: str, scan_root: Path) -> str | None:
   176→    """Resolve an absolute Python import within the project."""
   177→    parts = module_path.split(".")
   178→    # Try from scan root
   179→    target_base = scan_root.resolve()
   180→    for part in parts:
   181→        target_base = target_base / part
   182→
   183→    resolved = _try_resolve_path(target_base)
   184→    if resolved:
   185→        return resolved
   186→
   187→    # Try from project root
   188→    target_base = PROJECT_ROOT
   189→    for part in parts:
   190→        target_base = target_base / part
   191→
   192→    return _try_resolve_path(target_base)
   193→
   194→
   195→def _try_resolve_path(target_base: Path) -> str | None:
   196→    """Try to resolve a module base path to an actual file."""
   197→    # foo.py
   198→    candidate = Path(str(target_base) + ".py")
   199→    if candidate.is_file():
   200→        return str(candidate.resolve())
   201→
   202→    # foo/__init__.py
   203→    candidate = target_base / "__init__.py"
   204→    if candidate.is_file():
   205→        return str(candidate.resolve())
   206→
   207→    # foo/ (directory with __init__.py)
   208→    if target_base.is_dir():
   209→        init = target_base / "__init__.py"
   210→        if init.is_file():
   211→            return str(init.resolve())
   212→
   213→    return None

1→"""Python complexity signal compute functions.
     2→
     3→Used by ComplexitySignal definitions in __init__.py for the structural phase.
     4→"""
     5→
     6→import re
     7→
     8→
     9→def compute_max_params(content: str, lines: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str] | None:
    10→    """Find the function with the most parameters. Returns (count, label) or None."""
    11→    def_re = re.compile(r"def\s+\w+\s*\(", re.MULTILINE)
    12→    max_params = 0
    13→    for m in def_re.finditer(content):
    14→        # Track paren depth to find matching close-paren (handles nested parens)
    15→        depth = 1
    16→        start = m.end()
    17→        i = start
    18→        while i < len(content) and depth > 0:
    19→            ch = content[i]
    20→            if ch == "(":
    21→                depth += 1
    22→            elif ch == ")":
    23→                depth -= 1
    24→            i += 1
    25→        if depth != 0:
    26→            continue
    27→        param_str = content[start:i - 1]
    28→        params = [p.strip() for p in param_str.split(",") if p.strip()]
    29→        real_params = [p for p in params
    30→                       if p not in ("self", "cls") and not p.startswith("*")]
    31→        if len(real_params) > max_params:
    32→            max_params = len(real_params)
    33→    if max_params > 7:
    34→        return max_params, f"function with {max_params} params"
    35→    return None
    36→
    37→
    38→def _detect_indent_unit(lines: list[str]) -> int:
    39→    """Detect indentation unit from file content using GCD of indentations."""
    40→    from math import gcd
    41→    indents = set()
    42→    for line in lines:
    43→        stripped = line.lstrip()
    44→        if stripped and not stripped.startswith("#"):
    45→            indent = len(line) - len(stripped)
    46→            if 0 < indent <= 16:
    47→                indents.add(indent)
    48→    if not indents:
    49→        return 4
    50→    unit = 0
    51→    for i in indents:
    52→        unit = gcd(unit, i)
    53→    return max(unit, 1)
    54→
    55→
    56→def compute_nesting_depth(content: str, lines: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str] | None:
    57→    """Find maximum nesting depth by indentation. Returns (depth, label) or None."""
    58→    indent_unit = _detect_indent_unit(lines)
    59→    max_depth = 0
    60→    for line in lines:
    61→        stripped = line.lstrip()
    62→        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
    63→            continue
    64→        indent = len(line) - len(stripped)
    65→        depth = indent // indent_unit
    66→        if depth > max_depth:
    67→            max_depth = depth
    68→    if max_depth > 4:
    69→        return max_depth, f"nesting depth {max_depth}"
    70→    return None
    71→
    72→
    73→def compute_long_functions(content: str, lines: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str] | None:
    74→    """Find functions >80 LOC. Returns (longest_loc, label) or None."""
    75→    results = []
    76→    fn_re = re.compile(r"^(\s*)def\s+(\w+)")
    77→
    78→    i = 0
    79→    while i < len(lines):
    80→        m = fn_re.match(lines[i])
    81→        if not m:
    82→            i += 1
    83→            continue
    84→
    85→        fn_indent = len(m.group(1))
    86→        fn_name = m.group(2)
    87→        fn_start = i
    88→
    89→        j = i + 1
    90→        while j < len(lines):
    91→            if lines[j].strip() == "":
    92→                j += 1
    93→                continue
    94→            line_indent = len(lines[j]) - len(lines[j].lstrip())
    95→            if line_indent <= fn_indent and lines[j].strip():
    96→                break
    97→            j += 1
    98→
    99→        fn_loc = j - fn_start
   100→        if fn_loc > 80:
   101→            results.append((fn_name, fn_loc))
   102→        i = j
   103→
   104→    if results:
   105→        longest = max(results, key=lambda x: x[1])
   106→        return longest[1], f"long function ({longest[0]}: {longest[1]} LOC)"
   107→    return None
   108→

1→"""Python unused detection via ruff (F401=unused imports, F841=unused vars)."""
     2→
     3→import json
     4→import re

     6→from pathlib import Path

     8→from ....utils import PROJECT_ROOT
     9→from .... import utils as _utils_mod
    10→
    11→
    12→def detect_unused(path: Path, category: str = "all") -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    13→    """Detect unused imports and variables using ruff.
    14→
    15→    Falls back to pyflakes if ruff is not available.
    16→    Returns (entries, total_statements_checked).
    17→    """
    18→    from ....utils import find_py_files
    19→    total_files = len(find_py_files(path))
    20→
    21→    entries = _try_ruff(path, category)
    22→    if entries is not None:
    23→        return entries, total_files
    24→
    25→    entries = _try_pyflakes(path, category)
    26→    if entries is not None:
    27→        return entries, total_files
    28→
    29→    return [], total_files
    30→
    31→
    32→def _try_ruff(path: Path, category: str) -> list[dict] | None:
    33→    """Try ruff for unused detection."""
    34→    select = []
    35→    if category in ("all", "imports"):
    36→        select.append("F401")
    37→    if category in ("all", "vars"):
    38→        select.append("F841")
    39→    if not select:
    40→        return []
    41→
    42→    try:
    43→        result = subprocess.run(
    44→            ["ruff", "check", "--select", ",".join(select),
    45→             "--output-format", "json", "--no-fix", str(path)],
    46→            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, timeout=60,
    47→        )
    48→    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    49→        return None
    50→
    51→    if not result.stdout.strip():
    52→        return []
    53→
    54→    try:
    55→        diagnostics = json.loads(result.stdout)
    56→    except json.JSONDecodeError:
    57→        return None
    58→
    59→    entries = []
    60→    name_re = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")
    61→
    62→    for d in diagnostics:
    63→        code = d.get("code", "")
    64→        message = d.get("message", "")
    65→        filepath = d.get("filename", "")
    66→        if _utils_mod._extra_exclusions and any(_utils_mod.matches_exclusion(filepath, ex) for ex in _utils_mod._extra_exclusions):
    67→            continue
    68→        location = d.get("location", {})
    69→        line = location.get("row", 0)
    70→
    71→        # Extract name from message like "`foo` imported but unused"
    72→        m = name_re.search(message)
    73→        name = m.group(1) if m else message.split()[0]
    74→
    75→        cat = "imports" if code == "F401" else "vars"
    76→        if category != "all" and cat != category:
    77→            continue
    78→
    79→        # Skip _ prefixed names
    80→        if name.startswith("_"):
    81→            continue
    82→
    83→        entries.append({
    84→            "file": filepath,
    85→            "line": line,
    86→            "col": location.get("column", 0),
    87→            "name": name,
    88→            "category": cat,
    89→        })
    90→
    91→    return entries
    92→
    93→
    94→def _try_pyflakes(path: Path, category: str) -> list[dict] | None:
    95→    """Fallback: try pyflakes for unused detection."""
    96→    try:
    97→        result = subprocess.run(
    98→            ["pyflakes", str(path)],
    99→            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, timeout=60,
   100→        )
   101→    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
   102→        return None
   103→
   104→    entries = []
   105→    # pyflakes output: file.py:line: 'foo' imported but unused
   106→    import_re = re.compile(r"^(.+):(\d+):\d*\s+'([^']+)'\s+imported but unused")
   107→    var_re = re.compile(r"^(.+):(\d+):\d*\s+local variable '([^']+)' is assigned to but never used")
   108→
   109→    for line in (result.stdout + result.stderr).splitlines():
   110→        m = import_re.match(line)
   111→        if m and category in ("all", "imports"):
   112→            filepath = m.group(1)
   113→            if _utils_mod._extra_exclusions and any(_utils_mod.matches_exclusion(filepath, ex) for ex in _utils_mod._extra_exclusions):
   114→                continue
   115→            entries.append({
   116→                "file": filepath,
   117→                "line": int(m.group(2)),
   118→                "col": 0,
   119→                "name": m.group(3),
   120→                "category": "imports",
   121→            })
   122→            continue
   123→
   124→        m = var_re.match(line)
   125→        if m and category in ("all", "vars"):
   126→            filepath = m.group(1)
   127→            if _utils_mod._extra_exclusions and any(_utils_mod.matches_exclusion(filepath, ex) for ex in _utils_mod._extra_exclusions):
   128→                continue
   129→            entries.append({
   130→                "file": filepath,
   131→                "line": int(m.group(2)),
   132→                "col": 0,
   133→                "name": m.group(3),
   134→                "category": "vars",
   135→            })
   136→
   137→    return entries
   138→

1→"""Python extraction: function bodies, class structure, param patterns."""
     2→
     3→import hashlib
     4→import re
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from ...detectors.base import ClassInfo, FunctionInfo

    10→
    11→
    12→def _read_file(filepath: str) -> str | None:
    13→    """Read a file, returning None on error."""
    14→    p = Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else PROJECT_ROOT / filepath
    15→    try:
    16→        return p.read_text()
    17→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    18→        return None
    19→
    20→
    21→def _find_block_end(lines: list[str], start: int, base_indent: int,
    22→                    limit: int | None = None) -> int:
    23→    """Find end of an indented block. Returns first line at or below base_indent."""
    24→    end = limit if limit is not None else len(lines)
    25→    j = start
    26→    while j < end:
    27→        if lines[j].strip() == "":
    28→            j += 1
    29→            continue
    30→        if len(lines[j]) - len(lines[j].lstrip()) <= base_indent:
    31→            break
    32→        j += 1
    33→    return j
    34→
    35→
    36→def _find_signature_end(lines: list[str], start: int) -> int | None:
    37→    """Find the line where a function signature closes (')' then ':'). None if not found."""
    38→    for j in range(start, len(lines)):
    39→        lt = lines[j]
    40→        if ")" in lt and ":" in lt[lt.rindex(")") + 1:]:
    41→            return j
    42→        if j > start and lt.strip().endswith(":"):
    43→            return j
    44→    return None
    45→
    46→
    47→def extract_py_functions(filepath: str) -> list[FunctionInfo]:
    48→    """Extract function bodies from a Python file using indentation-based boundaries."""
    49→    content = _read_file(filepath)
    50→    if content is None:
    51→        return []
    52→
    53→    lines = content.splitlines()
    54→    functions = []
    55→    fn_re = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(?:async\s+)?def\s+(\w+)\s*\(")
    56→
    57→    i = 0
    58→    while i < len(lines):
    59→        m = fn_re.match(lines[i])
    60→        if not m:
    61→            i += 1
    62→            continue
    63→
    64→        fn_indent = len(m.group(1))
    65→        name = m.group(2)
    66→        start_line = i
    67→
    68→        # Find end of multi-line signature (closing ')' followed by ':')
    69→        j = _find_signature_end(lines, i)
    70→        if j is None:
    71→            i += 1
    72→            continue
    73→
    74→        # Extract params from multi-line signature
    75→        sig_text = "\n".join(lines[start_line:j + 1])
    76→        open_paren = sig_text.index("(")
    77→        close_paren = sig_text.rindex(")")
    78→        param_str = sig_text[open_paren + 1:close_paren]
    79→        params = extract_py_params(param_str)
    80→
    81→        # Find body extent: all lines indented past fn_indent, trim trailing blanks
    82→        block_end = _find_block_end(lines, j + 1, fn_indent)
    83→        end_line = block_end
    84→        while end_line > j + 1 and not lines[end_line - 1].strip():
    85→            end_line -= 1
    86→        body = "\n".join(lines[start_line:end_line])
    87→        normalized = normalize_py_body(body)
    88→
    89→        if len(normalized.splitlines()) >= 3:
    90→            functions.append(FunctionInfo(
    91→                name=name, file=filepath, line=start_line + 1,
    92→                end_line=end_line, loc=end_line - start_line, body=body,
    93→                normalized=normalized,
    94→                body_hash=hashlib.md5(normalized.encode()).hexdigest(),
    95→                params=params,
    96→            ))
    97→        i = end_line
    98→
    99→    return functions
   100→
   101→
   102→def normalize_py_body(body: str) -> str:
   103→    """Normalize a Python function body: strip docstrings, comments, print/logging."""
   104→    lines = body.splitlines()
   105→    normalized = []
   106→    in_docstring = False
   107→    docstring_quote = None
   108→
   109→    for line in lines:
   110→        stripped = line.strip()
   111→
   112→        if in_docstring:
   113→            if docstring_quote and docstring_quote in stripped:
   114→                in_docstring = False
   115→            continue
   116→
   117→        if stripped.startswith('"""') or stripped.startswith("'''"):
   118→            docstring_quote = stripped[:3]
   119→            if stripped.count(docstring_quote) >= 2:
   120→                continue
   121→            in_docstring = True
   122→            continue
   123→
   124→        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
   125→            continue
   126→
   127→        # Strip inline comments
   128→        cp = stripped.find("  #")
   129→        if cp > 0:
   130→            stripped = stripped[:cp].rstrip()
   131→
   132→        if re.match(r"(?:print\s*\(|(?:logging|logger|log)\.\w+\s*\()", stripped):
   133→            continue
   134→        if stripped:
   135→            normalized.append(stripped)
   136→
   137→    return "\n".join(normalized)
   138→
   139→
   140→def extract_py_classes(path: Path) -> list[ClassInfo]:
   141→    """Extract Python classes with method/attribute/base-class metrics (>=50 LOC)."""
   142→    results = []
   143→    for filepath in find_py_files(path):
   144→        content = _read_file(filepath)
   145→        if content is None:
   146→            continue
   147→        results.extend(_extract_classes_from_file(filepath, content.splitlines()))
   148→    return results
   149→
   150→
   151→def _extract_classes_from_file(filepath: str, lines: list[str]) -> list[ClassInfo]:
   152→    """Extract ClassInfo objects from a single Python file."""
   153→    results = []
   154→    class_re = re.compile(r"^class\s+(\w+)\s*(?:\(([^)]*)\))?\s*:")
   155→
   156→    i = 0
   157→    while i < len(lines):
   158→        m = class_re.match(lines[i])
   159→        if not m:
   160→            i += 1
   161→            continue
   162→
   163→        class_name = m.group(1)
   164→        bases = m.group(2) or ""
   165→        class_start = i
   166→        class_indent = len(lines[i]) - len(lines[i].lstrip())
   167→        class_end = _find_block_end(lines, i + 1, class_indent)
   168→        class_loc = class_end - class_start
   169→
   170→        if class_loc < 50:
   171→            i = class_end
   172→            continue
   173→
   174→        methods = _extract_methods(lines, class_start + 1, class_end, class_indent)
   175→        attributes = _extract_init_attributes(lines, class_start, class_end)
   176→        base_list = [b.strip() for b in bases.split(",") if b.strip()] if bases else []
   177→        non_mixin_bases = [b for b in base_list
   178→                           if not b.endswith("Mixin") and b not in ("object", "ABC")]
   179→
   180→        results.append(ClassInfo(
   181→            name=class_name, file=filepath, line=class_start + 1,
   182→            loc=class_loc, methods=methods, attributes=attributes,
   183→            base_classes=non_mixin_bases,
   184→        ))
   185→        i = class_end
   186→
   187→    return results
   188→
   189→
   190→def _extract_methods(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int,
   191→                     class_indent: int) -> list[FunctionInfo]:
   192→    """Extract methods from a class body as FunctionInfo objects."""
   193→    methods = []
   194→    method_re = re.compile(r"^\s+(?:async\s+)?def\s+(\w+)")
   195→
   196→    i = start
   197→    while i < end:
   198→        m = method_re.match(lines[i])
   199→        if not m:
   200→            i += 1
   201→            continue
   202→
   203→        method_indent = len(lines[i]) - len(lines[i].lstrip())
   204→        method_start = i
   205→        j = _find_block_end(lines, i + 1, method_indent, limit=end)
   206→        methods.append(FunctionInfo(
   207→            name=m.group(1), file="", line=method_start + 1,
   208→            end_line=j, loc=j - method_start, body="",
   209→        ))
   210→        i = j
   211→
   212→    return methods
   213→
   214→
   215→def _extract_init_attributes(lines: list[str], class_start: int,
   216→                              class_end: int) -> list[str]:
   217→    """Extract self.x = ... attribute names from __init__."""
   218→    attrs = set()
   219→    in_init = False
   220→    init_indent = 0
   221→
   222→    for k in range(class_start, class_end):
   223→        stripped = lines[k].strip()
   224→        if re.match(r"def\s+__init__\s*\(", stripped):
   225→            in_init = True
   226→            init_indent = len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip())
   227→            continue
   228→        if in_init:
   229→            if lines[k].strip() and len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip()) <= init_indent:
   230→                in_init = False
   231→                continue
   232→            for attr_m in re.finditer(r"self\.(\w+)\s*=", lines[k]):
   233→                attrs.add(attr_m.group(1))
   234→
   235→    return sorted(attrs)
   236→
   237→
   238→def extract_py_params(param_str: str) -> list[str]:
   239→    """Extract parameter names from a Python function signature."""
   240→    params = []
   241→    for token in " ".join(param_str.split()).split(","):
   242→        token = token.strip()
   243→        if not token or token in ("self", "cls"):
   244→            continue
   245→        name = token.lstrip("*").split(":")[0].split("=")[0].strip()
   246→        if name and name.isidentifier():
   247→            params.append(name)
   248→    return params
   249→
   250→
   251→def py_passthrough_pattern(name: str) -> str:
   252→    """Match same-name keyword arg: param=param in a function call."""
   253→    escaped = re.escape(name)
   254→    return rf"\b{escaped}\s*=\s*{escaped}\b"
   255→
   256→
   257→_PY_DEF_RE = re.compile(r"^def\s+(\w+)\s*\(", re.MULTILINE)
   258→
   259→
   260→def detect_passthrough_functions(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
   261→    """Detect Python functions where most params are same-name forwarded."""
   262→    entries = []
   263→    for filepath in find_py_files(path):
   264→        content = _read_file(filepath)
   265→        if content is None:
   266→            continue
   267→
   268→        for m in _PY_DEF_RE.finditer(content):
   269→            name = m.group(1)
   270→            # Track paren depth to find matching close-paren (handles nested parens)
   271→            depth = 1
   272→            i = m.end()
   273→            while i < len(content) and depth > 0:
   274→                ch = content[i]
   275→                if ch == "(":
   276→                    depth += 1
   277→                elif ch == ")":
   278→                    depth -= 1
   279→                i += 1
   280→            if depth != 0:
   281→                continue
   282→            param_str = content[m.end():i - 1]
   283→            params = extract_py_params(param_str)
   284→            if len(params) < 4:
   285→                continue
   286→
   287→            # Skip past return annotation and colon to get function body
   288→            rest_after_paren = content[i:]
   289→            colon_m = re.search(r":", rest_after_paren)
   290→            if not colon_m:
   291→                continue
   292→            rest = rest_after_paren[colon_m.end():]
   293→            bm = re.search(r"\n(?=[^\s\n#])", rest)
   294→            body = rest[:bm.start()] if bm else rest
   295→
   296→            has_kwargs_spread = bool(re.search(r"\*\*kwargs\b", body))
   297→            pt, direct = _classify_params(
   298→                params, body, py_passthrough_pattern, occurrences_per_match=2)
   299→
   300→            if len(pt) < 4 and not has_kwargs_spread:
   301→                continue
   302→
   303→            ratio = len(pt) / len(params)
   304→            classification = classify_passthrough_tier(
   305→                len(pt), ratio, has_spread=has_kwargs_spread)
   306→            if classification is None:
   307→                continue
   308→            tier, confidence = classification
   309→
   310→            entries.append({
   311→                "file": filepath, "function": name,
   312→                "total_params": len(params), "passthrough": len(pt),
   313→                "direct": len(direct), "ratio": round(ratio, 2),
   314→                "line": content[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1,
   315→                "tier": tier, "confidence": confidence,
   316→                "passthrough_params": sorted(pt),
   317→                "direct_params": sorted(direct),
   318→                "has_kwargs_spread": has_kwargs_spread,
   319→            })
   320→
   321→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (-e["passthrough"], -e["ratio"]))
   322→

   260→def _find_external_test_files(path: Path, lang_name: str) -> set[str]:

   271→            continue  # test_dir is inside scanned path, zone_map already has it

   275→        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
   276→            for f in files:
   277→                if isinstance(ext, tuple):
   278→                    if any(f.endswith(e) for e in ext):
   279→                        extra.add(os.path.join(root, f))
